cars.blurb: The Mazda 787 and its derivative 787B are Group C sports prototype racing cars that were developed by Japanese automobile manufacturer Mazda for use in the World Sportscar Championship, All Japan Sports Prototype Championship, and the 24 Hours of Le Mans from 1990 to 1991. Designed to combine a mixture of the Fédération Internationale du Sport Automobile (FISA) Group C regulations with the International Motor Sports Association (IMSA) GTP regulations, the 787s were the last Wankel rotary-powered racing cars to compete in the World and Japanese championships, using Mazda's R26B engine.

cars.name: Eunos Cosmo
cars.blurb: The Eunos Cosmo was the final generation of the Mazda Cosmo, which served as Mazda's flagship vehicle in Japan and was sold through its luxury Eunos division. During its production run the Cosmo served as a "halo" vehicle for Mazda.

cars.name: Autozam AZ-1
cars.blurb: The Autozam AZ-1 (known by the framecode PG6SA) is a sports car which was manufactured by Mazda from October 1992 to October 1994 and sold under its Autozam brand. Suzuki provided the engine as well as the inspiration for the design. It is a two-seater kei car with a rear mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout and gullwing doors. Power came from the same Suzuki-sourced 657 cc turbocharged engine used by the Suzuki Alto that produced 64 PS (47 kW) at 6,500 rpm and 85 N⋅m (63 lb⋅ft) at 4,000 rpm. The top speed was electronically governed to be 140 km/h (87 mph).

specs.designer: Tatsumi Fukunaga (Suzuki RS/3); Toshihiko Hirai (design leader)

cars.name: Mazda MX-3 V6
cars.blurb: The Mazda MX-3 is a 2+2-seat, front-wheel drive coupé of a kammback design, manufactured and marketed by Mazda. It was introduced at the Geneva Auto Show in March 1991 and marketed until 1998. The MX-3 was also marketed as the Mazda MX-3 Precidia in Canada and as the Eunos Presso, Autozam AZ-3 and Mazda AZ-3 in Japan. In Australia it was marketed as the Eunos 30X until late 1996 when it became the Mazda-Eunos 30X.

specs.engine: 1.5 L B5-ZE I4 DOHC; 1.6 L B6-ME I4 SOHC; 1.6 L B6D I4 DOHC; 1.8 L K8 V6 DOHC

cars.name: Mazda Bongo
cars.blurb: The Mazda Bongo (Japanese: マツダ・ボンゴ, Hepburn: Matsuda Bongo), also known as the Ford Econovan and Eunos Cargo, is a cabover van and pickup truck manufactured by the Japanese automobile manufacturer Mazda since 1966. The Bongo name was also used for the Bongo Friendee, which is not a cabover design. It has been built with rear-, middle-, as well as front-mounted engines.

specs.layout: Rear-engine, rear-wheel-drive (1966–1975) ; Front mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive (1977–present) ; Front mid-engine, four-wheel-drive (1983–present)

cars.name: Mazda RX-8
cars.blurb: The Mazda RX-8 is a sports car manufactured by Japanese automobile manufacturer Mazda between 2003 and 2012. It was first shown in 2001 at the North American International Auto Show. It is the direct successor to the RX-7. Like its predecessors in the RX range, it is powered by a rotary Wankel engine. The RX-8 was available for the 2003 model year in most parts of the world.

cars.name: Subaru 360
cars.blurb: The Subaru 360 is a rear-engined, two-door city car manufactured and marketed by Subaru from 1958 to 1971. As the company's first mass-produced automobile, production reached 392,000 over its 12-year model run. Noted for its small overall size, 450 kg (1,000 lb) curb weight, monocoque construction, swing axle rear suspension, fiberglass roof panel, and rear-hinged doors, the inexpensive car was designed in response to the Japanese government's light car or Kei car regulations and its proposal for a larger "national car," both intended to help motorize the post WWII Japanese population. The 360's overall size and engine capacity complied with Japan's Kei car regulations.

specs.engine: 356 cc EK31 I2; 356 cc EK32 I2; 423 cc EK51 I2

cars.name: Subaru Sambar
cars.blurb: The Subaru Sambar is a cabover truck and microvan manufactured and marketed by Subaru as Japan's second truck compliant with the country's strict Keitora (軽トラ) or Kei vehicle tax class, after the Kurogane Baby. Introduced in 1961 in microvan and Kei pickup configurations, the Sambar remains in production, now in its eighth generation — beginning with the seventh generation as a rebadged Daihatsu Hijet.

cars.name: Subaru Leone (second generation)
cars.blurb: From Wikipedia's article on Subaru Leone: The Subaru Leone is a compact car produced by the Japanese car manufacturer Subaru from 1971 to 1994. The word leone is Italian for lion. It was released as a replacement for the Subaru 1000 and was the predecessor of the Subaru Impreza. All Leones were powered by the Subaru EA boxer engine.

cars.name: Subaru BRAT
cars.blurb: The Subaru BRAT is a four-wheel drive coupé utility by Subaru from 1978 to 1994, based on the Leone. Depending on the market it was known as the Brumby, MV Pickup or Shifter.

cars.name: Subaru XT
cars.blurb: The Subaru XT is a 2+2 car manufactured and marketed by Subaru from 1985 to 1991, with a facelift in 1987. It is a two-door coupé with a front-mounted engine and either front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. When the XT debuted, it was the most aerodynamic car in the US market.

specs.designer: Tetsuya Hayashi, Kiyoshi Sugimoto, Hiroshi Yako (interior)

cars.name: Subaru Justy

photos.artist: Quadmachine The original uploader was Quadmachine at English Wikipedia .

cars.blurb: The Subaru Justy is a subcompact hatchback manufactured and marketed by Japanese automaker Subaru since 1984. The company has marketed a rebadged variant known as the Daihatsu Boon (second generation), at the 2007 Frankfurt Motor Show with could be optioned with a 1.0 or 1.2-litre inline-3 engine, front/four wheel drive, electronically controlled continuously variable transaxle, or a 5-speed manual transaxle.

cars.name: Subaru Legacy (first generation)
cars.blurb: The first generation Subaru Legacy is a mid-size family car / wagon developed by Fuji Heavy Industries. The Legacy was an all new model, and was considered a notable departure from Subaru products in the past.

specs.engine: 1.6 L EJ16 H4 ; 1.8 L EJ18 H4 ; 2.0 L EJ20E H4 ; 2.0 L EJ20D DOHC H4 ; 2.0 L EJ20G DOHC turbo H4 ; 2.2 L EJ22/E H4 ; 2.2 L EJ22T turbo H4
specs.layout: FF layout standard ; F4 layout optional

cars.name: Subaru SVX
cars.blurb: The Subaru SVX, marketed in the Japanese home market as the Subaru Alcyone SVX, is a two-door, front-engine, all- or front-wheel drive coupé manufactured and marketed by Subaru from 1991 to 1996 over a single generation. Superseding the company's aviation-influenced XT range, the SVX was Subaru's first entry into the luxury/performance market, and was noted for its aircraft-inspired 'window-within-a-window' side-glass configuration. The nameplate "Alcyone" (pronounced "al-SIGH-uh-nee") refers to the brightest star in the Pleiades constellation, stylized in the Subaru company logo.

specs.layout: Front-engine, four-wheel drive; Front-engine, front-wheel drive

cars.name: Subaru Impreza WRX (GC8)
cars.blurb: From Wikipedia's article on Subaru Impreza: The Subaru Impreza (Japanese: スバル・インプレッサ, Hepburn: Subaru Inpuressa) is a compact car that has been manufactured by the Japanese automaker Subaru since 1992. It was introduced as a replacement for the Leone, with the predecessor's EA series engines replaced by the new EJ series.

cars.name: Subaru Impreza WRC
cars.blurb: The Subaru Impreza WRC is a World Rally Car based on the Subaru WRX.

cars.name: Subaru Outback (first generation)
cars.blurb: The first-generation Subaru Outback was derived from the wagon variant of the second-generation Legacy, and was called the "Legacy Grand Wagon" in Japan in 1995 and the "Legacy Outback" in most other markets. It added partial protective plastic side body cladding and a raised roof to the Legacy wagon, and would later raise the suspension.

cars.name: Subaru Impreza WRX STI (second generation)
cars.blurb: The second generation of the Subaru Impreza compact car was introduced in 2000 and manufactured up to 2007 by Subaru in Ōta, Gunma, Japan, in both sedan (GD series) and five-door Hatchback (GG series) bodystyles, as well as two intermediate facelifts throughout its lifespan.

specs.engine: 1.5 L EJ15 F4; 1.5 L EL15 F4; 1.6 L EJ16 F4; 2.0 L EJ20 F4; 2.0 L EJ20 F4 (Turbo); 2.5 L EJ25 F4; 2.5 L EJ25 F4 (Turbo)
specs.designer: Hidefumi Kato (1998); Peter Stevens (2001) (2003 Facelift); Andreas Zapatinas (2004) (2005 Facelift)

cars.name: Subaru BRZ

photos.artist: Charles from Port Chester, New York
Charles from Port Chester, New York

cars.blurb: The Subaru BRZ and the Toyota 86 are 2+2 sports cars jointly developed by Toyota and Subaru, manufactured at Subaru's Ōta, Gunma assembly plant. The BRZ's name comes from three elements: Boxer engine, rear-wheel drive, and Z standing for Zenith. It differs from the 86 in the front fascia, with a different grille and headlight assembly, and a different front wing vent.

cars.name: Subaru WRX STI (VA)
cars.blurb: The Subaru WRX STI (VA) was released in 2014 alongside the VA WRX.

cars.name: Mitsubishi Model A
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Model A is the only car built by the Mitsubishi Shipbuilding Company, a member of the Mitsubishi corporate group which would eventually evolve into Mitsubishi Motors, and the first series production automobile manufactured in Japan.

cars.name: Mitsubishi 500
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi 500 was the first passenger car produced after the Second World War by Shin Mitsubishi Heavy-Industries, Ltd, one of the companies which would become Mitsubishi Motors. It was built from 1960 until 1962 and formed the basis for Mitsubishi's next model, the Colt 600. It was exported in small numbers. Correspondance from 1999 indicates just eight surviving vehicles.

specs.engine: 493 cc NE19A OHV I2; 594 cc NE35A OHV I2
specs.designer: Masataka Nimura, Munetaro Shigehiro, Tsutomu Ieda

cars.name: Mitsubishi Colt Galant GTO
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Colt Galant GTO (Gran Turismo Omologato) is an automobile which was produced by Mitsubishi Motors from 1970 to 1977. It was first shown as the Galant GTX-1 showcar at the 1969 Tokyo Motor Show. Sales began in November 1970, when it was the flagship hardtop variant of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries's then-new Colt Galant sedan.

cars.name: Mitsubishi Lancer 1600 GSR
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Lancer (A70) is the first generation version of Mitsubishi's long-running Lancer nameplate. When introduced in 1973, it filled the gap between the Minica kei car and the considerably larger Galant. It was a replacement for the Colt 1200, last sold in 1970. Although sedan production ended in 1979, vans continued on until 1985.

cars.name: Mitsubishi Delica
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Delica (Japanese: 三菱・デリカ, Hepburn: Mitsubishi Derika) is a range of vans and pickup trucks designed and built by the Japanese automaker Mitsubishi Motors since 1968. It was originally based on a cabover van and pickup truck introduced the previous year, also called the Delica, its name a contraction of the English language phrase Delivery car.

specs.layout: Front-mid engine, rear-wheel-drive (1968–present); Front-mid engine, four-wheel-drive (1979–1994); Front-engine, rear-wheel-drive (1994–present); Front-engine, front-wheel-drive (2007–present); Front-engine, four-wheel-drive (1994–present)

cars.name: Mitsubishi Pajero (first generation)
cars.blurb: The first production version of the Mitsubishi Pajero debuted at the 1981 Tokyo Motor Show before sales officially began in 1982. The name derives from Leopardus pajeros, the Pampas cat. Mitsubishi marketed the SUV as the Montero in North America, Spain, and most of Latin America because "pajero" is derogatory in Spanish.

cars.name: Mitsubishi Pajero Evolution
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Pajero Evolution is an off-road competition car based on the Mitsubishi Pajero. It was specially designed to take part in the rally raids with the main objective of winning the Dakar Rally. In addition to those produced for competition use only, a road-legal version was manufactured by Mitsubishi from 1997 to 1999 in order to homologate the Pajero Evolution for the Dakar Rally's T2 class.

cars.name: Mitsubishi Starion
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Starion is a sports car which was manufactured and marketed by Mitsubishi from 1982 until 1989 — with badge engineered variants marketed in North America as the Conquest, under the Chrysler, Dodge, and Plymouth brands. It is a two-door coupé with a fastback design and seating for four passengers.

specs.engine: 2.0 L G63B I4 ; 2.0 L G63B turbo I4 ; 2.6 L G54B turbo I4
specs.designer: Ryu Kaibuchi, Takashi Kono, Masaki Iwamoto, Hidetoshi Aoki

cars.name: Mitsubishi Galant VR-4
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Galant VR-4 first appeared with the sixth-generation Galant, and was the basis for Mitsubishi's participation in the 1988-1992 World Rally Championships. For 1992, the emergence of the homologated Lancer Evolution meant that the top-spec Galant VR-4 was no longer constrained by sporting regulations.

cars.name: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution I to III
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution III was among the Lancer Evolutions that were successful in WRC rallies from 1996 to 1999, mostly in the hands of Finnish driver Tommi Mäkinen, who clinched driver's titles in four consecutive seasons from 1996 to 1999 (in Evolutions III, IV, V, and VI).

cars.name: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution IV to IX
cars.blurb: From Wikipedia's article on Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution: The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution, popularly referred to as the "Lancer Evo", "LanEvo" or "Evo", is a sports sedan and rally car based on the Lancer that was manufactured by Japanese manufacturer Mitsubishi Motors from 1992 until 2016.

cars.name: Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution X
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution X is the tenth and final generation of the Lancer Evolution, a sports sedan produced by Japanese manufacturer Mitsubishi Motors, designed by Omer Halilhodžić. By September 2005, Mitsubishi introduced a concept version of the next-gen Evolution at the 39th Tokyo Motor Show named the Concept-X, designed by Omer Halilhodžić at the company's European design centre.

cars.name: Mitsubishi 3000GT and GTO
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi 3000GT is a front-engine, all-wheel/front-wheel drive grand touring/sports car manufactured and marketed by Mitsubishi from 1990 until 2000 over three different series. Manufactured in a three-door hatchback coupé body style in Nagoya, Japan, the 2+2 four-seaters were marketed in the Japanese domestic market as the GTO, and globally as 3000GT. In North America, it was sold both as the Mitsubishi 3000GT (1991–1999) and the Dodge Stealth (1991–1996), a badge engineered, mechanically identical captive import.

specs.engine: 3.0 L 6G72 SOHC V6 ; 3.0 L 6G72 DOHC 24v V6 ; 3.0 L 6G72 DOHC 24v twin-turbocharged V6

cars.name: Mitsubishi Eclipse (first generation)
cars.blurb: The first-generation Mitsubishi Eclipse was marketed as an entry to the mid-level four-cylinder sports coupe segment and was available in five trim levels. It received updated, more ovoid sheet metal for 1992, when exposed aerodynamic headlights replaced the pop-up units, and was replaced by the second generation for the 1995 model year.

cars.name: Mitsubishi FTO
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi FTO is a front-engined, front-wheel drive sport compact car produced by Mitsubishi Motors between 1994 and 2000.

specs.engine: 1.8 L 4G93 SOHC 16V I4 ; 2.0 L 6A12 DOHC 24V V6 ; 2.0 L 6A12 DOHC 24V MIVEC V6

cars.name: Mitsubishi i-MiEV
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi i-MiEV (MiEV is an acronym for Mitsubishi innovative Electric Vehicle) is a five-door electric city car produced in the 2010s by Mitsubishi Motors, and is the electric version of the Mitsubishi i. Rebadged variants of the i-MiEV are also sold by PSA as the Peugeot iOn and Citroën C-Zero, mainly in Europe. The i-MiEV was the world's first modern highway-capable mass production electric car.

cars.name: Suzuki Suzulight
cars.blurb: Suzulight (Japanese: スズライト) was the brand used for kei cars built by the Suzuki Motor Corporation from 1955 to 1969. They were Suzuki's first entry into automotive manufacturing, having previously only produced motorcycles. It was Japan's second front-wheel drive car, after the very limited production Tsukuba-go of the 1930s.

cars.name: Suzuki Carry
cars.blurb: The Suzuki Carry (Japanese: スズキ・キャリイ, Hepburn: Suzuki Kyarī) is a kei truck produced by the Japanese automaker Suzuki. The microvan version was originally called the Carry van until 1982 when the passenger van versions were renamed as the Suzuki Every (Japanese: スズキ・エブリイ, Hepburn: Suzuki Eburī).

cars.name: Suzuki Samurai
cars.blurb: The Suzuki Samurai was an updated version of the SJ413 and the first Suzuki officially marketed in the US. The nameplate "Samurai", derived from samurai warriors, was introduced first in 1985 in North America. The difference in width is the only major difference between SJ and Samurai, apart from some minor cosmetic changes in the interior and the exterior.

cars.name: Suzuki Alto (first generation)

photos.artist: Niels de Wit from Lunteren, The Netherlands

cars.blurb: The Suzuki Alto was first introduced in 1979 as a commercial vehicle derivative of the Fronte, available only as a three-door "light van" with bare-bones equipment. Over time the nameplate gained in popularity, and by 1988 it replaced the Fronte name completely.

cars.name: Suzuki Cappuccino
cars.blurb: The Suzuki Cappuccino (Japanese: スズキ・カプチーノ, Suzuki Kapuchīno) is a sports car produced by the Japanese company Suzuki from 1991 to 1998. It is a two-seater roadster with a detachable hardtop that is designed to meet Japanese kei car regulations.

specs.engine: 657 cc F6A DOHC turbo I3 ; 657 cc K6A DOHC turbo I3

cars.name: Suzuki X-90
cars.blurb: The Suzuki X-90 is a rear- or four-wheel drive, two-door, two-seater offroad automobile incorporating sports car elements, manufactured and marketed by Suzuki between 1995 and 1997. Derived from the Suzuki Vitara, the X-90 featured a T-top removable roof. Replacing the Samurai in the United States market. Suzuki began marketing the X-90 in Japan toward the end of 1995, and in western markets in April 1996.

cars.name: Suzuki Vitara (first generation)
cars.blurb: The name of the Suzuki Vitara was inspired by the Latin word vita, as in the English word vitality. For the 1996 model year Suzuki introduced the X-90, which was mechanically identical to the Vitara but had a much rounder, two-seater body with a separate boot and removable T-bar roof.

cars.name: Suzuki Wagon R
cars.blurb: The Suzuki Wagon R (Japanese: スズキ・ワゴンR, Suzuki Wagon'āru) is a kei car manufactured and marketed by Suzuki since 1993. The R in the name stands for Revolution and Relaxation. The Wagon R uses a "tall wagon" configuration to maximize cabin space within kei car dimensional restrictions. The Wagon R is also sold by Mazda as the AZ-Wagon from 1994 to 2012 and as the Flair from 2012.

cars.name: Suzuki Swift Sport
cars.blurb: The Suzuki Swift Sport is powered by an enhanced M16A unit, a high-revving 1.6-liter, naturally aspirated DOHC VVT four-cylinder engine with an 11.1:1 compression ratio. It features sportier bumpers and spoilers, a stiffer suspension, twin exhaust pipes and four-wheel disc brakes on 16-inch wheels.

cars.name: Suzuki Jimny (fourth generation)
cars.blurb: The Suzuki Jimny (fourth generation) was launched as an all-new model in late 2018. It is again available with a stretched wheelbase (34 cm / 13.4 in) and a five-door configuration. Like all four Jimny generations, it has a separate body and ladder frame.

cars.name: Daihatsu Midget
cars.blurb: The Daihatsu Midget (Japanese: ダイハツ・ミゼット, Hepburn: Daihatsu Mizetto) is a single-seater mini-truck, later a microvan/kei truck made by Japanese automaker Daihatsu. Several distinct vehicles have borne the Midget name over the years, but all have had in common a single or two-seat utilitarian design, with an enclosed or semi-enclosed cab.

cars.name: Daihatsu Hijet
cars.blurb: The Daihatsu Hijet (Japanese: ダイハツ・ハイゼット, Hepburn: Daihatsu Haizetto), is a cab over microvan and kei truck produced and sold by the Japanese automaker Daihatsu since 1960. The Daihatsu Atrai (Japanese: ダイハツ・アトレー, Hepburn: Daihatsu Atorē), a passenger-specific version, was introduced in 1981.

cars.name: Daihatsu Fellow Max
cars.blurb: The Daihatsu Fellow Max is a small Japanese automobile in the Kei car class. Originally introduced as the Daihatsu Fellow, the name was partially retained for its successor, the Max Cuore (1977), and then revived in 2000 for the Daihatsu Max.

cars.name: Daihatsu Charade (G11)
cars.blurb: The second-generation Daihatsu Charade (G11) was released in March 1983, again as a three- or five-door hatchback. The G11 was produced with square headlights (Series 1) and rectangular "cat's eye" headlights (Series 2). For China it was known as the Tianjin TJ730, built as a CKD from 1986 to 1988.

cars.name: Daihatsu Charade De Tomaso Turbo
cars.blurb: The Daihatsu Charade De Tomaso and the Charade Turbo had the upgraded 1.0-litre "CB" series engine, called the CB50 and CB60. At the 1981 Tokyo Motor Show, Daihatsu displayed a 1-liter turbo car concept in collaboration with Italian sports car maker De Tomaso Automobili.

cars.name: Daihatsu Rocky and Feroza
cars.blurb: The Daihatsu Rocky (Japanese: ダイハツ・ロッキー, Hepburn: Daihatsu Rokkī) is an automobile nameplate used by the Japanese automobile manufacturer Daihatsu since 1984 for three different SUV models: Daihatsu Rocky (F70), an export version of the Rugger sold between 1984 and 2002 Daihatsu Rocky (F300), a ladder frame-based mini SUV sold in Japan and some international markets between 1989 and 2002 Daihatsu Rocky (A200), a subcompact crossover sold since 2019 The Rocky was popular in Australia in the 1980s and 1990s, largely drawing from the success in Japan, where it was known as the Lovibond Rocky.

cars.name: Daihatsu Mira
cars.blurb: The Daihatsu Mira (also known as the Cuore, Domino, and more recently Charade) was a kei-type city car built by Japanese car maker Daihatsu. It was built with a variety of options and chassis variations, with the latest variant having four models: Mira, Mira AVY, Mira Gino, and Mira VAN.

cars.name: Daihatsu Copen
cars.blurb: The Daihatsu Copen (Japanese: ダイハツ・コペン, Daihatsu Kopen) is a 2-door convertible kei car built by the Japanese car company Daihatsu. It debuted at the 1999 Tokyo Motor Show, as the Daihatsu Copen concept. The second generation model debuted as the Kopen (Future Included) at the 2013 Tokyo Motor Show.

cars.name: Daihatsu Naked
cars.blurb: The Daihatsu Naked (Japanese: ダイハツ・ネイキッド, Hepburn: Daihatsu Neikiddo) is a kei car built by the Japanese automaker Daihatsu from 1999 to 2003. It was first presented as a concept at the 1997 Tokyo Motor Show, while the production ready model was shown there in 1999.

specs.engine: 658 cc EF-VE I3 ; 658 cc EF-DET turbo I3

cars.name: Isuzu Bellel
cars.blurb: The Isuzu Bellel is a compact car produced by the Japanese automobile manufacturer Isuzu from 1961 to 1967. It was the company's first independent design, and also Japan's first passenger car with a diesel engine. It was available as a four-door sedan and a five-door station wagon, called the Bellel Express. The Bellel Express was technically speaking a commercial vehicle, as was the custom in Japan at the time.

specs.engine: petrol: ; 1491 cc GL150 I4 OHV (PA10) ; 1949 cc G200 I4 OHV (PA10) ; diesel: ; 1999 cc DL200 I4 (PAD10) ; 1991 cc DL201 I4 (PAD10)

cars.name: Isuzu 117 Coupe
cars.blurb: The Isuzu 117 Coupé is a compact Gran Turismo type 2-door fastback coupé which was produced by the Japanese automobile manufacturer Isuzu between 1968 and 1981. 117 was the codename for a common development program of Isuzu mid-size cars, involving a coupé, sedan, and station wagon. The latter two eventually became the Isuzu Florian, but the coupé kept the original name. The two ranges shared mechanicals, including the complete FR layout chassis with recirculating ball steering.

cars.name: Isuzu Bellett GT-R
cars.blurb: The Isuzu Bellett GT-R, more specifically GT Type-R (for "racing"), was a racing version of the GT, also available to individual customers. First presented in September 1969, it featured a 1.6 L DOHC engine from the 117 Coupé, power brakes and numerous other modifications.

cars.name: Isuzu Piazza
cars.blurb: The Isuzu Piazza is a small, sporty 3-door liftback coupé which was manufactured by Isuzu from 1981–1993 across two generations, marketed also as the Isuzu Impulse in North America and as the Holden Piazza in Australia. The first generation Piazza used rear-wheel drive and in the United Kingdom it was the first widely available Isuzu passenger car.

cars.name: Isuzu Trooper
cars.blurb: The Isuzu Trooper is a mid-size SUV manufactured and marketed by Isuzu between September 1981 and September 2002 over two generations, the first, produced between 1981 and 1991; and the second (UBS) produced between 1991 and 2002, the latter with a mid-cycle refresh in 1998. In its earliest iterations, the Trooper was based on the company's first generation Isuzu Faster/Chevrolet LUV pickup.

cars.name: Isuzu VehiCROSS
cars.blurb: The Isuzu VehiCROSS is a compact SUV manufactured by Isuzu from 1997 through 2001 (Japanese market 1997–1999; US market 1999–2001). The Isuzu VehiCROSS share a platform with the short wheelbase variant Isuzu Trooper second generation.

specs.production: 1997–2001 (5,958 units) ; 1,805 units in Japan ; 4,153 units in United States
specs.designer: Shiro Nakamura and Satomi Murayama (chief designer); Simon Cox, Joji Yanaka, Andrew Hill and Nick Robinson

cars.name: Hino Contessa
cars.blurb: The Hino Contessa is an automobile which was produced by Hino Motors from 1961 to 1967. The Contessa was developed largely from the 1947–1961 Renault 4CV powertrain under license to Hino Motors. Offered in both coupe and sedan bodystyles, it replaced the Hino Renault, which was the Renault 4CV manufactured by Hino for Japan.

cars.name: Mitsuoka Viewt
cars.blurb: The Mitsuoka Viewt (Japanese: 光岡・ビュート, Hepburn: Mittsuoka Byūto) is a series of retro-styled subcompact cars sold by the Japanese automaker Mitsuoka, intended to resemble the 1963 Jaguar Mark 2. The Viewt is Mitsuoka's best selling model. It was initially a modification of the Nissan March until 2023, when the March was replaced by the Note.

cars.name: Mitsuoka Orochi
cars.blurb: The Mitsuoka Orochi (Japanese: 光岡大蛇) is a Japanese sports car designed and built by Mitsuoka Motors as a concept car in 2001, with updates and revisions to the design appearing in 2003 and 2005, before finally being put into production and offered for sale in late 2006 as a 2007 model. The car takes its name from the mythical Yamata no Orochi 8-headed Japanese dragon.

cars.name: Dome Zero
cars.blurb: The Dome Zero (童夢-零, Dōmu Zero) was a prototype sports car from DOME Co. Ltd that was exhibited at the 48th Geneva Auto Show in 1978. The Dome project, pronounced "do-mu" or "child's dream" in Japanese, was started by Minoru Hayashi in 1975, with the goal of producing sports cars using knowledge gained from auto racing.

cars.name: ASL Garaiya
cars.blurb: The ASL Garaiya (Japanese: ASL・ガライヤ, Hepburn: ASL Garaiya) is a mid-engined concept sports car developed by ASL, the car manufacturing arm of Autobacs Seven.

cars.name: Toyota FJ Cruiser
cars.blurb: The Toyota FJ Cruiser (Japanese: トヨタ・FJクルーザー, Hepburn: Toyota Efujē Kurūzā) is a retro-styled mid-size SUV produced by Toyota between 2006 and 2022. Introduced as a concept car at the January 2003 North American International Auto Show, the FJ Cruiser was approved for production after positive consumer response and debuted at the February 2005 Chicago Auto Show in final production form.

cars.name: Toyota Soarer (Z20)
cars.blurb: The Z20 series Toyota Soarer was produced from January 1986 to April 1991 and was available in several variants. It was based on the A70 series Supra platform, though unlike the A70 Supra it was not offered with the 2.5 L twin turbo 1JZ-GTE. The third-generation Z30 series Soarer replaced it in Japan.

cars.name: Toyota Mark II (X90)
cars.blurb: The Toyota Mark II X90 series was a redesigned Mark II released in October 1992. The X90 series was available in six different trim levels.

cars.name: Subaru Forester (first generation)
cars.blurb: The first-generation Subaru Forester was built on the platform of the Impreza in the style of a taller station wagon. It was introduced as the Streega concept at the 1995 Tokyo Motor Show and went on sale in Japan in February 1997, reaching the U.S. market later that year for the 1998 model year.

cars.name: Honda CR-V (first generation)

photos.artist: Guyon from Richmond, VA, United States of America

cars.blurb: The first-generation Honda CR-V, or RD1, was Honda's first in-house designed sport utility vehicle, by Hiroyuki Kawase. Initial models were built using the same platform as the Civic. Until 2001, the CR-V sold more than any other vehicle in its class.

cars.name: Honda Odyssey (first generation)
cars.blurb: From Wikipedia's article on Honda Odyssey: Honda Odyssey can refer to three motor vehicles manufactured by Honda: Honda Odyssey (ATV), an all-terrain vehicle (1977—1989) Honda Odyssey (minivan), a brand of two different Honda minivan models for different markets Honda Odyssey (international), sold in Japan and most other parts of the world Honda Odyssey (North America), sold primarily in North America and certain other markets

cars.name: Nissan Cube (second generation)
cars.blurb: The second-generation Nissan Cube was released in 2002 with a larger interior than the previous model. Its design was previewed by the Nissan Chappo Concept shown at the 2001 Geneva Motor Show. A slightly longer, three-row model, the Cube³, went on sale in September 2003.

cars.name: Nissan Stagea 260RS
cars.blurb: The Nissan Stagea is a station wagon produced by Nissan from 1996 to 2007. It was originally produced by Nissan in 1996 as direct competition for the Subaru Legacy Touring wagon in Japan, and was exclusive to Nissan Prince Store Japanese dealerships.

specs.layout: Front-engine, rear-wheel-drive / all-wheel-drive (1996–2001); Front mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive / all-wheel-drive (2001–2007)

cars.name: Mitsubishi Minica
cars.blurb: The Mitsubishi Minica (Japanese: 三菱・ミニカ, Hepburn: Mitsubishi Minika) is a model series of kei cars, produced by Mitsubishi Motors Corp. (MMC) over five generations, from 1962 to 2011, mainly for the Japanese domestic market. The Minica was first built by Shin Mitsubishi Heavy-Industries, one of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' three regional automotive companies, until they were merged in 1964.

cars.name: Ferrari 250 GTO
cars.blurb: The 250 GTO was Ferrari's V12 grand tourer, built from 1962 to 1964 to homologate for the FIA's Group 3 category, whose rules asked for at least 100 cars. Ferrari persuaded the rule makers to count the earlier 250 GT SWB, so just 36 GTOs were made. Collectors want it badly, and sales have repeatedly set price records.

nuggets.text: A popular myth says that when FIA inspectors came to confirm 100 cars had been built, Enzo Ferrari shuffled the same cars between locations to make it look as though all of them were there.
In June 2018 a 1963 car, chassis 4153GT, sold privately to David MacNeil for $70 million, the current record for the world's most expensive Ferrari.

specs.engine: 2,953 cc ; Tipo 168 Comp/62 60º V12 ; SOHC 2 valves per cylinder valvetrain configuration ; 6 Weber 38 DCN carburetors ; Compression ratio 9.7:1

cars.name: Ferrari 250 GT California Spyder
cars.blurb: The 250 GT California Spyder is the open-top version of Ferrari's contemporary Berlinetta, styled by Sergio Scaglietti and built by Carrozzeria Scaglietti around a Ferrari V12. About 100 were made, split almost evenly between long-wheelbase cars from 1957 to 1960 and short-wheelbase cars from 1960 to 1963. The 1986 film Ferris Bueller's Day Off brought it considerable recognition.

nuggets.text: A short-chassis California once owned by Roger Baillon, and lost to history for nearly 30 years, sold at Artcurial in 2015 for 14,200,000 euros before auction fees.
In 2008 television host Chris Evans paid a record 7,040,000 euros at a Sotheby's auction for a car that actor James Coburn had owned.

specs.engine: 3.0 L (2953.21 cc) Colombo Tipo 128 and 168 V12

cars.name: Dino 206 and 246 GT
cars.blurb: The Dino 206 GT, 246 GT and 246 GTS were V6 mid-engined sports cars built by Ferrari and sold under the Dino marque between 1967 and 1974. The 246 was the first car Ferrari made in high numbers, with 3,569 built, and Motor Trend Classic placed the 206/246 at number seven among its 10 greatest Ferraris of all time.

nuggets.text: A Dino 246 GTS won the Cannonball Baker Sea-to-Shining-Sea Memorial Trophy Dash in 1975.
The 206 GT was the first car Ferrari sold with electronic ignition, a system Magneti Marelli developed for the high-revving Dino V6.

cars.name: Ferrari Daytona
cars.blurb: The Daytona was Ferrari's two-seat grand tourer of 1968 to 1973, introduced at the Paris Auto Salon to replace the 275 GTB/4. It used the 275's Colombo V12, bored out to 4,390 cc, and came as the 365 GTB/4 coupe and the 365 GTS/4 convertible, 1,284 and 122 built. Leonardo Fioravanti drew it at Pininfarina, and Scaglietti built the production bodies.

nuggets.text: Ferrari itself only rarely calls the 365 a Daytona, and refers to the name as unofficial.
A Daytona replica was prominently featured in the first two seasons of NBC's Miami Vice in the 1980s.

cars.name: Ferrari 308 GTB/GTS
cars.blurb: The 308 was Ferrari's mid-engine V8 two-seater, sold from 1975 to 1985 as the GTB berlinetta and the targa-topped GTS. Leonardo Fioravanti drew it at Pininfarina. It replaced the Dino 246 GT and GTS and gave way to the 328 in 1985. A smaller-engined 208 version was sold mainly in Italy.

nuggets.text: Only 808 fibreglass-bodied cars were made, all of them berlinettas.
Thomas Magnum, played by Tom Selleck, drove a 308 around Oahu through eight seasons of Magnum, P.I., from 1980 to 1988.

cars.name: Ferrari Testarossa
cars.blurb: The Testarossa, a Pininfarina-styled mid-engine coupé with a 4.9 litre flat-12, premiered at the 1984 Paris Auto Show as the successor to the Berlinetta Boxer. Its name pays homage to the 250 Testa Rossa that won the 1957 World Sportscar Championship. With the 512 TR and F512 M revisions it ran to 1996, and 9,939 were built, a high count for a Ferrari at the time.

nuggets.text: Don Johnson, who drove a white Testarossa on Miami Vice, was given a brand-new silver 1989 Testarossa by Enzo Ferrari himself, who was a fan of the show.
Miami Vice and Sega's 1986 video game Out Run helped popularize the Testarossa, a recognized cultural icon of the 1980s.

specs.designer: Diego Ottina, Leonardo Fioravanti, Ian Cameron, Guido Campoli, Emanuele Nicosia at Pininfarina (Testarossa); Pietro Camardella at Pininfarina (512 TR)

cars.name: Ferrari F40
cars.blurb: The F40 was designed to celebrate Ferrari's 40th anniversary and was the last Ferrari personally approved by Enzo Ferrari. Nicola Materazzi engineered the mid-engine, rear-drive car around a twin-turbocharged 2,936 cc V8, with styling by Pininfarina. At the time it was Ferrari's fastest, most powerful and most expensive car for sale, listed at about US$400,000, fivefold the price of the 288 GTO.

nuggets.text: Formula One driver Nigel Mansell's car sold for a then-record 1 million pounds in 1990, a record that stood into the 2010s.
It was estimated in 1990 that only 10% of the delivered F40s were being used for driving.

specs.designer: Pietro Camardella under the supervision of Aldo Brovarone at Pininfarina; Nicola Materazzi (Chief Engineer)

cars.name: Ferrari F50
cars.blurb: The F50 was a limited-production, mid-engine Ferrari built from 1995 to 1997, with 349 made. Its 4.7 litre naturally aspirated V12 was developed from the 3.5 litre V12 in the 1990 Ferrari 641 Formula One car, and Pininfarina took design cues from contemporary F1 cars, particularly at the front. The engine predated the car, having been used in the 333 SP in 1994.

nuggets.text: Following the lead of the F40 LM, Ferrari developed the F50 GT, a prototype based on the F50 and built to compete in GT1-class racing.

specs.designer: Pietro Camardella and Lorenzo Ramaciotti at Pininfarina

cars.name: Enzo Ferrari
cars.blurb: The Enzo, officially Enzo Ferrari, is a mid-engine sports car named for the company's founder and built from 2002 to 2004. It was developed with Formula One technology, including a carbon-fibre body, an F1-style automated manual gearbox and carbon-ceramic disc brakes, plus active aerodynamics, which F1 does not allow. Ken Okuyama of Pininfarina designed it around a new 6.0 litre V12.

nuggets.text: In 2004 the 400th production car was built and donated to the Vatican for charity, and was later sold at a Sotheby's auction for US$1.1 million.
The Enzo was described as one of the "Fifty Ugliest Cars of the Past 50 Years", with Bloomberg Businessweek citing its curves and angles as too flashy.

specs.designer: Ken Okuyama at Pininfarina; Frank Stephenson (FXX)

cars.name: LaFerrari
cars.blurb: LaFerrari means "The Ferrari" in Italian, and Ferrari intended it as the definitive Ferrari. It is a limited-production, mid-engine, mild hybrid sports car with a 6.3 litre V12, built from 2013 to 2018 as a coupé and later as the Aperta targa.

nuggets.text: In 2017 the last LaFerrari Aperta was auctioned for charity for US$10 million.
Its design received no input from Pininfarina, making it the first Ferrari since the Bertone-styled 1973 Dino 308 GT4 without Pininfarina bodywork.

specs.designer: Ferrari Styling Centre under Flavio Manzoni

cars.name: Lamborghini 350 GT
cars.blurb: The 350 GT was the first production car from Lamborghini, a grand tourer with a 3.5 litre V12 and a two-door coupé body by Carrozzeria Touring. It debuted at the March 1964 Geneva Motor Show, production began that May, and 120 were built. Its success ensured the company's survival and established it as a viable rival to Ferrari.

nuggets.text: Ferruccio wanted an engine "good for 40,000 hard miles between services", so Dallara and Wallace de-tuned a version of the GTV prototype motor for street use.

cars.name: Lamborghini Miura
cars.blurb: The Miura was the first high-performance production road car with a rear mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout, which has since become the standard for performance sports cars. When released it was the fastest production car in the world. Marcello Gandini styled it at Bertone around a transverse 3,929 cc V12, and 764 were made between 1966 and 1973.

nuggets.text: Miles Davis owned a Miura and crashed it in October 1972 while turning off the West Side Highway, breaking both his ankles and totaling the car.
The Bertone Miura Roadster was the only factory open-top Miura, though a few other cars have had their tops removed.

cars.name: Lamborghini Espada
cars.blurb: The Espada was a four-seat grand touring coupé built by Lamborghini from 1968 to 1978, with 1,227 made. Marcello Gandini designed it at Bertone, and it carried a front-mounted 3,929 cc V12 driving the rear wheels. A prototype was built by Bertone and the factory after the 1967 debut of the Marzal, which inspired the first-series dashboard.

nuggets.text: One Espada was fitted with a prototype hydropneumatic self-levelling rear suspension called Lancomatic.

cars.name: Lamborghini Countach
cars.blurb: The Countach is a rear mid-engine Lamborghini built from 1974 to 1990, drawn by Marcello Gandini at Bertone in the sharply angled Italian Wedge style. The prototype appeared as the LP500 at the 1971 Geneva Motor Show, and three years of refinement produced the LP400 of 1974. The basic shape stayed virtually unchanged over its 19-year lifespan, while its V12 grew from 3,929 to 5,167 cc.

nuggets.text: The upward-opening doors first appeared on Gandini's 1968 Alfa Romeo Carabo concept, attached by horizontal hinges at the front of the door so they lifted up and tilted forward.
The nose slope was made shallower because excessive front-end downforce destabilized the prototype under braking.

specs.engine: Lamborghini V12; LP400, LP400 S: 3929 cc ; LP500 S: 4754 cc ; 5000 QV, 25th Anniversary: 5167 cc

cars.name: Lamborghini Diablo

designer_note.gandini: Initial design; final design by Chrysler under Tom Gale

cars.blurb: The Diablo was Lamborghini's V12 mid-engine supercar, built from 1990 to 2001, and the first production Lamborghini with a top speed above 200 mph. The 1993 VT was the company's first all-wheel-drive production sports car, able to send up to 25% of torque to the front wheels. A roadster followed in 1995, Lamborghini's first open-top V12. In all, 2,903 were built.

nuggets.text: The Diablo is named after a ferocious bull raised by the Duke of Veragua in the 19th century, famous for an epic fight with 'El Chicorro' in Madrid on 11 July 1869.
A second SV roadster was completed on 6 April 1998 in Giallo Orion, bringing that variant to two units and making it the rarest series-production Lamborghini ever built.

specs.layout: Longitudinal, Mid-engine, rear-wheel drive / all-wheel drive
specs.designer: Marcello Gandini (initial design) ; Tom Gale at Chrysler Styling Center (final design) ; Luc Donckerwolke (Diablo VT 6.0)

cars.name: Lancia Aurelia

designer_note.pininfarina: B24 convertible design and B50 cabriolet
designer_note.ghia: B20 coupe body design, built by Pininfarina

cars.blurb: The Lancia Aurelia ran from 1950 to 1958 over six series, as a saloon, a cabriolet, the B20 GT coupé, the B24 spider and a rolling chassis for coachbuilders. It is noted for using one of the first series-production V6 engines. Lancia named it after the Via Aurelia, the Roman road from Rome to Pisa, and built 18,201.

nuggets.text: Modified Aurelias took the first three places in the 1952 Targa Florio, with Felice Bonetto the winner, and won Liège-Rome-Liège in 1953.
The Aurelia is prominent in The Calculus Affair, one of the Tintin adventures, in the story's car chase scene.

specs.engine: 1.8 L tipo B10 V6 ; 2.0 L tipo B15/B20/B21/B22 V6 ; 2.3 L tipo B12 V6 ; 2.5 L tipo B20/B24 V6
specs.designer: Felice Mario Boano at Ghia (B20 coupé); Pinin Farina (B24 convertible)

cars.name: Lancia Fulvia
cars.blurb: The Fulvia was a front-wheel-drive Lancia with a V4 engine, introduced at the Geneva Motor Show in 1963 and built until 1976 as a Berlina saloon, a Coupé and the Zagato-built Sport fastback. It is named after the Via Fulvia, the Roman road from Tortona to Turin. It won the 1972 International Rally Championship, and Road & Track called it "a precision motorcar, an engineering tour de force".

nuggets.text: The first Sport, introduced at the 1965 Turin Motor Show, had an all-aluminium alloy bodyshell and used the coupé's 1.2 litre engine.
A special edition based on the 1.3 S commemorated Lancia's victory at the 1972 Monte Carlo Rally.

specs.engine: petrol: ; 1,091 cc Lancia V4 ; 1,199 cc Lancia V4 ; 1,216 cc Lancia V4 ; 1,231 cc Lancia V4 ; 1,298 cc Lancia V4 ; 1,584 cc Lancia V4
specs.designer: Piero Castagnero at Centro Stile Lancia (Berlina and Coupé); Ercole Spada at Zagato (Sport)

cars.name: Lancia Stratos
cars.blurb: The Stratos HF was a rear mid-engine car that Lancia designed for rallying, styled by Marcello Gandini at Bertone. It was the first car designed from scratch for the sport, and it won the World Rally Championship in 1974, 1975 and 1976, plus the 1974 Targa Florio. Production ran from 1973 to 1978, about 492 cars, powered by a Ferrari Dino V6.

nuggets.text: Enzo Ferrari was reluctant to sign off on the engine for a car he saw as a competitor to his own Dino V6, though its use had been planned from the start of the project.

cars.name: Lancia 037
cars.blurb: The Lancia 037, homologated as 151 ARO, is a mid-engine car built in the early 1980s for Group B of the World Rally Championship. It was the first car built specifically for Group B and the last rear-wheel-drive car to win the WRC. It took the manufacturers' world championship for Lancia in 1983. Enrico Fumia styled it at Pininfarina.

nuggets.text: Besides the 1983 World Championship, the 037 won European Rally Championship titles in 1983, 1984 and 1985, and Italian titles in 1983 and 1985.

specs.designer: Enrico Fumia at Pininfarina (styling); Sergio Limone (project leader); Pier Paolo Messori (technical director)

cars.name: Lancia Delta Integrale

designer_note.italdesign: Parent Delta of 1979, not the Integrale changes
designer_note.giugiaro: Parent Delta of 1979, not the Integrale changes

cars.blurb: The Delta HF integrale was a four-wheel-drive sports model of Lancia's Delta. Its four-wheel-drive system, shared with the Delta HF 4WD, was based on the one developed for the 1985 Lancia Delta S4 Group B rally car, though in a transverse front-engine rather than a longitudinal mid-engine layout. The HF integrale 16v was due to be replaced at the end of 1991 by the HF integrale Evoluzione.

nuggets.text: The four-wheel-drive system in every HF integrale was based on the one developed for the 1985 Lancia Delta S4 Group B rally car, albeit in a transverse front-engine instead of a longitudinal mid-engine layout.

cars.name: Alfa Romeo 8C

photos.artist: Brian Snelson from Hockley, Essex, England

cars.blurb: The Alfa Romeo 8C was a family of 1930s road, race and sports cars built around a straight-eight designed by Vittorio Jano, which served as Alfa's primary racing engine from 1931 to 1939. It powered the Monoposto Tipo B, the world's first genuine single-seat Grand Prix car, and later the twin-engined Bimotore. Touring bodied a Spider and a Berlinetta for the road.

nuggets.text: Tazio Nuvolari won the 1935 German Grand Prix at the Nürburgring in a 3.2 litre Tipo B, against the more powerful Silver Arrows of Mercedes-Benz and Auto Union.
A former Scuderia Ferrari 8C 35, in which Nuvolari won the 1936 Coppa Ciano, sold in September 2013 for 5.9 million pounds, a world record for any Alfa Romeo.

specs.engine: 2.3 L 2336 cc I8; 2.6 L 2556 cc I8; 2.9 L 2905 cc I8; (road cars)

cars.name: Alfa Romeo Giulietta
cars.blurb: The Giulietta was a family of Alfa Romeos built from 1954 to 1965, including a 2+2 coupé, a saloon, an estate, a spider and the Sprint Speciale. The first to appear was the Sprint 2+2 coupé at the 1954 Turin Motor Show, and it was Alfa's first successful foray into the 1.3 litre class. In all, 177,690 were made.

nuggets.text: Hoffman received the first 600 Spiders built, so American buyers had the Spider for quite some time before Italians could get one.
The Sprint Veloce took the first three places in its class at the 1956 Mille Miglia.

specs.designer: Franco Scaglione at Bertone (Sprint, Sprint Speciale); Pinin Farina (Spider); Ercole Spada at Zagato (SZ)

cars.name: Alfa Romeo Spider
cars.blurb: The Alfa Romeo Spider was a two-seat, front-engined, rear-drive roadster built in four series from 1966 until April 1993, nearly three decades, as successor to the Giulia Spider. Aldo Brovarone and Battista Pininfarina designed it at Pininfarina. The last one was the final rear-wheel-drive Alfa Romeo before the 8C Competizione of 2007.

nuggets.text: The 1600 Spider was the last project in which Pininfarina's founder, Battista Pininfarina, was involved.
For North America a model called the Graduate acknowledged the car's appearance in the 1967 film The Graduate, starring Dustin Hoffman.

specs.designer: Aldo Brovarone and Battista Pininfarina at Pininfarina

cars.name: Alfa Romeo 33 Stradale
cars.blurb: The 33 Stradale was a mid-engine Alfa Romeo road car derived from the Tipo 33 sports prototype, with a 2.0 litre V8, a six-speed Colotti gearbox and a weight of 700 kg. Franco Scaglione designed it, and 18 were built between 1967 and 1969. It was the fastest commercially available car for the standing kilometer on its introduction, and the most expensive car on sale in 1968, at US$17,000.

nuggets.text: In 1968 Germany's Auto, Motor und Sport measured 24.0 seconds for the standing kilometer, making it the fastest commercially available car over that distance at the time.
A 33 Stradale can be seen in the 1969 Italian movie Un bellissimo novembre.

cars.name: Alfa Romeo Montreal
cars.blurb: The Alfa Romeo Montreal was a front-engine, rear-drive 2+2 coupé built from 1970 to 1977, designed by Marcello Gandini at Bertone and assembled in Turin. It had a 2.6 litre DOHC V8 and a five-speed ZF gearbox. The engine was inspired by the 2-litre V8 of the 33 Stradale and Tipo 33, but shares no parts with them.

nuggets.text: The slats behind the doors hold the cabin vents, but otherwise serve only cosmetic purposes.

cars.name: Alfa Romeo SZ

builder_note.zagato: Built with Zagato; styled in-house at Fiat Centro Stile, not by Zagato

cars.blurb: The Alfa Romeo SZ, short for Sprint Zagato, was a limited-production sports car built from 1989 to 1991 through a partnership of Centro Stile Zagato, Centro Stile Alfa Romeo and Centro Stile Fiat. It was first shown as the ES-30 prototype at the 1989 Geneva Motor Show. A 2,959 cc Busso V6 drove the rear wheels through a five-speed manual, in a coupé weighing 1,260 kg.

specs.designer: Centro Stile Fiat:; Robert Opron; Antonio Castellana

cars.name: Fiat 500
cars.blurb: Launched in July 1957 as the Nuova 500, successor to the Topolino, the Fiat 500 was an inexpensive and practical small car. Its original rear-mounted 479 cc two-cylinder air-cooled engine sat in a body just 2,970 mm long, and it is considered one of the first purpose-designed city cars. Production reached 3,893,294 by 1975.

nuggets.text: The 500 F is perhaps most associated with the Japanese franchise Lupin III. The car has gone with the eponymous character since the 1971 series Lupin the 3rd Part 1, and has been most prominently linked to the franchise since the 1979 film The Castle of Cagliostro.
Only the 1958-61 500N was officially sold in North America, yet the little Fiat was a popular gray-market import in the 1960s and 1970s, with private imports in the thousands.

cars.name: Fiat 124 Sport Spider
cars.blurb: The Fiat 124 Sport Spider was a front-engined, rear-drive convertible with a monocoque body, shown at the November 1966 Turin Auto Show with styling by Tom Tjaarda. Fiat sold it through 1982, including as the Spider 2000 from 1979, and Pininfarina carried on until 1985 as the Spider Azzurra for North America and the Spidereuropa for Europe.

nuggets.text: The 124 won the 1972 European Rally Championship at the hands of Raffaele Pinto and Gino Macaluso.
The double overhead cam version of the engine was the first mass-manufactured DOHC to use reinforced-rubber timing belts, an idea that came into nearly universal use over the following decades.

specs.engine: 1438 cc I4; 1592 cc I4; 1608 cc I4; 1756 cc I4; 1995 cc I4; 1995 cc turbo I4; 1995 cc sc I4
specs.designer: Pininfarina:; Tom Tjaarda (designer); Franco Martinengo (design director); Battista Pininfarina

cars.name: Fiat X1/9
cars.blurb: The Fiat X1/9 was a two-seat, mid-engined sports car designed by Bertone, built by Fiat from 1972 to 1982 and by Gruppo Bertone until 1989. Its transverse engine drove the rear wheels, and it was noted for balanced handling, retractable headlights and a light removable hardtop that stowed under the bonnet. It was also the first Fiat designed from the start to meet US safety regulations.

nuggets.text: In 1975 Dallara chose the X1/9 to enter the World Championship for Makes, in the Group 5 Special Production class.
Fiat's other models of the time carried numbers such as 127, 128, 124 and 131, showing their place in the range. The X1/9 kept its prototype code as its marketing name.

cars.name: Maserati 3500
cars.blurb: The Maserati 3500 GT (Tipo 101) was a grand tourer built in Modena from 1957 to 1964, offered as a 2+2 coupé and as a two-seat Spyder. It was Maserati's first successful attempt at the Gran Turismo market and at series production. A 3.5-litre straight-six powered it, and 2,226 were made.

nuggets.text: The first Touring prototype was a white 2+2 of superleggera construction, nicknamed Dama Bianca, or White Lady.
The main development work was done in 1956 and 1957, even as Maserati was busy with its Formula 1 world championship entry.

specs.designer: Carrozzeria Touring (coupé); Giovanni Michelotti at Vignale (spyder)

cars.name: Maserati Ghibli
cars.blurb: The original Ghibli, Tipo AM115, was a V8-engined two-door 2+2 grand tourer built by Maserati from 1967 to 1973. Its name is the Libyan Arabic word for the hot, dry south-westerly wind of the Libyan Desert. A two-seat Spyder joined the fastback coupé in 1969, and the Bertone-designed Khamsin followed in 1974.

nuggets.text: The Ghibli first appeared as a two-seat concept car at the Turin Motor Show in November 1966.
The production car added two rear seats that were nothing more than cushions without backrests, which let Maserati market it as a 2+2 fastback coupé.

cars.name: Maserati Bora
cars.blurb: The Maserati Bora (Tipo AM117) was a two-seat, rear mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive sports car and grand tourer built from 1971 to 1978 and named for the wind of Trieste. It was Maserati's first mid-engined street car and its first with four-wheel independent suspension, and it ended the company's reputation for fast but technologically out of date cars. Giorgetto Giugiaro of Italdesign designed it, and 564 were built.

nuggets.text: The development prototype and the 1971 Geneva show car used MacPherson struts at the front, but the layout was dropped for production because of a severe drivability issue.

specs.engine: 4719 cc Tipo AM 107.07 V8 ; 4930 cc Tipo AM 107.16 V8

cars.name: Maserati MC12
cars.blurb: The Maserati MC12 was a limited-production two-seater built in 2004 and 2005 so that a racing version could compete in the FIA GT Championship. It sits on the chassis of the Ferrari Enzo but wears a larger body with a lower drag coefficient. Twenty-five cars were built in 2004 and 25 shorter ones in 2005, giving 50 for customers and 62 in all with the racers.

nuggets.text: On Top Gear, The Stig lapped the Top Gear track in 1:18.9 in an MC12, a tenth of a second quicker than his lap in the Enzo Ferrari.
In 2005 Maserati won the FIA GT Manufacturers Cup with 239 points, almost double the 125 of the next competitor, Ferrari.

cars.name: De Tomaso Mangusta
cars.blurb: The De Tomaso Mangusta was a sports car built in Modena from 1967 to 1971, with 401 made. Giorgetto Giugiaro drew the coupé body at Ghia around a rear mid-mounted Ford V8, of either 4,728 cc or 4,942 cc, and a ZF five-speed manual. The Pantera succeeded it.

specs.engine: 4728 cc Ford 289 V8 ; 4942 cc Ford 302 V8

cars.name: De Tomaso Pantera
cars.blurb: The De Tomaso Pantera, Italian for Panther, was a mid-engine sports car built from 1971 to 1992 and the maker's most popular model, with over 7,000 made. Tom Tjaarda designed it at Ghia around a Ford V8, and its steel monocoque was the first De Tomaso built that way. More than three quarters of production were sold by American Lincoln-Mercury dealers from 1972 to 1975.

nuggets.text: The first 75 cars were essentially European imports, known for their push-button door handles and hand-built Carrozzeria Vignale bodies.
The first Group 4 Panteras were entered in the 1972 24 Hours of Le Mans.

specs.engine: 302 CID Ford 302 V8 (Pantera SI) ; 351 CID Ford Cleveland V8 ; 351 CID Ford Windsor V8 (1988–1990)
specs.designer: Tom Tjaarda at Ghia ; Marcello Gandini (Pantera SI)

cars.name: Iso Grifo
cars.blurb: The Iso Grifo was a limited-production grand tourer built between 1965 and 1974 to take on Ferrari and Maserati, using American Chevrolet and Ford power trains. Giorgetto Giugiaro styled it at Bertone and Giotto Bizzarrini handled the mechanicals. The first GL models of 1965 had Chevrolet 327 V8s, and the Series II of 1970 brought sleeker lines, hide-away headlights and a 7.4-litre 454 V8.

nuggets.text: In 1964 the prototype A3/C raced at Le Mans with Edgar Berney and Pierre Noblet driving, and ran well until brake problems forced a two-hour pit stop.
Only fourteen Series I Targas and four Series II Targas were built.

specs.engine: 5.4 L Chevrolet 327 OHV V8 ; 5.8 L Ford 351 OHV V8 ; 7.0 L Chevrolet 427 OHV V8 ; 7.4 L Chevrolet 454 OHV V8

cars.name: Bizzarrini 5300 GT
cars.blurb: The Bizzarrini Strada, also called the 5300 GT, was a low-slung two-seat sports car built from 1964 to 1968 and sold as a coupé, a roadster and the track-tuned Corsa racer. Giotto Bizzarrini designed it around a 5,358 cc Chevrolet 327 V8 with a four-speed Borg-Warner manual. It proved to be Bizzarrini's most successful model, with 133 built.

nuggets.text: Three Spyders were built. The prototype is painted silver, while the other two have removable T-tops with a center bar running through the roof.

cars.name: Pagani Zonda
cars.blurb: The Pagani Zonda is a mid-engined sports car, built mainly of carbon fibre, that debuted at the 1999 Geneva Motor Show and was built to order in small numbers. Horacio Pagani designed it around Mercedes-Benz V12 engines of 6.0 to 7.3 litres, in coupé, roadster and barchetta forms. By 2019 a total of 140 had been built, development mules included.

nuggets.text: The Zonda was first going to be called the Fangio F1, after Formula One champion Juan Manuel Fangio. After his death in 1995 it was renamed for the Zonda, a hot air current above Argentina.
The crash test and homologation car, chassis 001, was restored by Pagani's Rinascimento program and shown at the 2019 Geneva Motor Show for the Zonda's 20th anniversary.

specs.production: 1999–2019 (special edition/one-off models still occasionally built in limited numbers)
specs.engine: 6.0 – 7.3 L Mercedes-Benz M120 V12 ; 7.3 L Mercedes-Benz M297 V12

cars.name: Ford Model T
cars.blurb: The Ford Model T was built from October 1, 1908, to May 26, 1927, and is generally regarded as the first mass-affordable automobile. Assembly-line production helped cut the price from $780 in 1910 to $290 in 1924, putting car travel within reach of middle-class Americans. The 1999 Car of the Century competition named it the most influential car of the 20th century.

nuggets.text: A Parisian Ford dealer, Charles Montier, and his brother-in-law Albert Ouriou entered a heavily modified Model T, the Montier Special, in the first three 24 Hours of Le Mans.
On May 26, 1927, Henry Ford and his son Edsel drove the 15-millionth Model T out of the factory.

specs.designer: Childe Harold Wills, main-engineer Joseph A. Galamb and Eugene Farkas

cars.name: Duesenberg Model J

photos.artist: Steve Ginn from Western Washington, United States

cars.blurb: The Duesenberg Model J was an ultra-luxury car that debuted in 1928, intended to compete with the most luxurious and powerful cars in the world. It carried a 420 cubic-inch DOHC straight-eight with an optional supercharger, and bodies were coachbuilt to the owner's preference. In all, 481 were produced, and Duesenberg Motors went bankrupt in 1937.

nuggets.text: A Duesenberg SSJ once owned by Gary Cooper sold at auction in 2018 for $22 million.
The first example made, J-101, was a silver and black LeBaron sweep panel dual cowl phaeton. At the time of the New York presentation it was the only one.

specs.engine: 420 cuin DOHC Duesenberg Straight-8 engine, optional supercharger

cars.name: Cord 810/812

photos.artist: Brian Snelson from Hockley, Essex, England

cars.blurb: The Cord 810, and later the 812, was a luxury car built by Cord, a division of Auburn, in 1936 and 1937. It was the first American-designed and built front-wheel-drive car with independent front suspension, and the first production car with hidden pop-up headlights. Its nose dropped the traditional grille for horizontal louvers wrapped around the sides, earning the nickname 'coffin nose'.

nuggets.text: A single 814 prototype was built and sat in storage for many years until it was discovered in 1989.
In the 1938 film Gangster's Boy, starring Jackie Cooper, the main character drives a white 1937 Cord 812SC Sportman.

specs.engine: 288.6 cu in (4.7 L) Lycoming FB V8
specs.designer: Gordon Buehrig, Vince Gardner, Alex Tremulis

cars.name: Tucker 48
cars.blurb: The Tucker 48, also known as the Tucker Torpedo, was conceived by Preston Tucker and built in Chicago in 1948. It was a rear-engined sedan with four-wheel independent suspension and a horizontally opposed six. Only 51 cars were made, counting the prototype, before the company was forced to stop operations on March 3, 1949 after bad publicity, an SEC investigation and a stock fraud trial that ended in full acquittal.

nuggets.text: Film director Francis Ford Coppola was a Tucker owner and displayed his car on the grounds of his winery.
Tucker #1043 sold for $2.915 million at auction in 2012.

specs.engine: boxer-6 (horizontally opposed), OHV, 334.1 cuin (4.50" bore × 3.50" stroke), 7.0:1 compression ratio, 166 bhp, 372 lbft torque
specs.layout: Rear engine, rear-wheel drive, 4-wheel independent suspension (rubber torsion tube (no springs) with shock absorbers)
specs.designer: George S. Lawson, Alex Tremulis, Read Viemeister, Budd Steinhilber, Tucker Madawick, Hal Bergstrom, Philip S. Egan

cars.name: Chevrolet Bel Air
cars.blurb: The Chevrolet Bel Air was a full-size Chevrolet sold for the 1950 to 1981 model years. Until 1952 the name marked only two-door hardtops; from 1953 it became a premium trim level across several body styles. By the time US production ended in 1975 it had become a budget fleet sedan, and Canada kept building it through the 1981 model year.

nuggets.text: A black 1955 Chevrolet Bel Air was featured in the 1973 movie American Graffiti.
A 1956 Bel Air four-door hardtop prepared by Chevrolet engineer Zora Arkus-Duntov set a new endurance and speed record for an automobile climbing Pikes Peak.

cars.name: Chevrolet Corvette (C1)
cars.blurb: The first-generation Corvette arrived late in the 1953 model year and ran through 1962. It is called the solid-axle generation because independent rear suspension waited until the 1963 Sting Ray. Rushed into production, it got mixed reviews and sales well short of expectations, and General Motors nearly cancelled the program, improving the car instead because Ford was developing the two-seater that became the Thunderbird.

nuggets.text: The 1953 model year was the Corvette's first production year, and at 300 built it was also the lowest-volume Corvette.

specs.engine: 235 CID Blue Flame I6; 265 CID Small-block V8; 283 CID Small-block V8 ; 327 CID Small-block V8

cars.name: Chevrolet Corvette (C2)
cars.blurb: The second-generation Corvette ran from the 1963 through 1967 model years and was built in St. Louis. Its engines ranged from 327 cubic-inch small-blocks to 427 big-blocks, and it was offered as a convertible or a coupe. The 1963 Sting Ray brought a new design and sharper handling, and the first-ever production Corvette coupe had a fastback body.

nuggets.text: Motor Trend timed a 1964 fuel-injected four-speed coupe with the 4.11:1 axle through the quarter-mile in 14.2 seconds at 100 mph, and from 0 to 60 mph in 5.6 seconds.
The split rear window is usually credited to Mitchell, who said he was inspired by the 57SC Bugatti Atlantique coupe.

cars.name: Chevrolet Corvette (C3)

designer_note.bill-mitchell: Chief stylist; GM and Chevrolet design staff

cars.blurb: The third-generation Corvette covers the 1968 to 1982 model years, with engines and chassis parts mostly carried over from the previous generation under an all-new body and interior. It set a sales record of 53,807 cars for 1979, and carried the Stingray name, now one word, from 1969 to 1976. A 1969 L88 Lightweight, one of four built, sold at Barrett-Jackson in January 2014 for $2,860,000.

nuggets.text: In 2023 RM Sotheby's Arizona auctioned one of two factory-produced 1969 Corvette ZL-1s for $3,140,000.
Only 53 ZR1s were built from 1970 to 1972: 25 in 1970, including 8 convertibles, then 8 in 1971 and 20 in 1972.

specs.designer: GM & Chevrolet design staff; Dave McLellan (chief engineer); Bill Mitchell (chief stylist)

cars.name: Chevrolet Corvette (C4)
cars.blurb: The fourth-generation Corvette covers the 1984 to 1996 model years. No 1983 Corvette went on sale, but GM built 43 pre-production pilot cars and ordered all but one destroyed. That white survivor is now on display at the National Corvette Museum in Bowling Green, Kentucky, and is described as the only true 1983 Corvette. The convertible returned in 1986.

nuggets.text: In early March 1990 the ZR1 set records for the highest average speed over 24 hours and over 5,000 miles.
The Callaway SledgeHammer, a derivative of the Twin Turbo Corvette, recorded a speed on Ohio's Transportation Research Center track in 1988 that made it the fastest road-going car at the time.

specs.engine: 350 cuin L83 V8 ; 350 cuin L98 V8 ; 350 cuin LT1 V8 ; 350 cuin LT4 V8 ; 350 cuin LT5 V8
specs.designer: Jerry Palmer under Dave McLellan (1980) and Irv Rybicki

cars.name: Chevrolet Corvette (C5)
cars.blurb: The fifth-generation Corvette ran for the 1997 to 2004 model years and included the high-performance Z06. It was the first GM vehicle with third-generation small-block LS engines and the last Corvette generation with pop-up headlights. The convertible, arriving for 1998, was the first to offer a trunk since 1962. The racing C5-R was a 24 Hours of Daytona and 24 Hours of Le Mans GTS/GT1 winner.

nuggets.text: When production ended on July 2, 2004, the C5 and the Lotus Esprit were the last cars overall to use pop-up headlamps. The last Esprit had left its line on February 20, 2004.
The C5 was the first Corvette with parallel windshield wipers, dropping the opposed arrangement used on every Corvette since the first in 1953.

cars.name: Ford Thunderbird (first generation)
cars.blurb: The first-generation Ford Thunderbird was a two-seat convertible built for the 1955 to 1957 model years, the first two-seat Ford since 1938. Ford called it a personal car of distinction. It was built largely from existing components and offered a standard V8, but it put driver comfort ahead of speed and was not a direct rival to the Corvette or European sports cars.

nuggets.text: Ford planned only 10,000 but sold 16,155, with a listed retail price of US$2,944 in 1955.
The 1957 Thunderbird was the last two-seater Ford sold until the 1982 Ford EXP.

specs.engine: 292 cuin Y-block V8; 312 cuin Y-block V8

cars.name: AC Cobra (Shelby Cobra)
cars.blurb: Sold in the United States as the Shelby Cobra, the AC Cobra paired a British AC Cars roadster with a Ford V8. It was built intermittently in the UK and later the US from 1962 to 1967, at Thames Ditton in Surrey and at Shelby American in Los Angeles. Production came to 655 leaf-spring cars and 343 coil-spring cars.

nuggets.text: The S/C, short for semi-competition, can sell for US$1.5 million for an original example, which makes it one of the most valuable Cobra variants.
Shelby offered a drag racing package called the Dragon Snake, which won several NHRA National events with Bruce Larson or Ed Hedrick driving CSX2093.

cars.name: Pontiac GTO
cars.blurb: The Pontiac GTO is a rear-drive, two-door, four-passenger car from the Pontiac division of General Motors, built over four generations from 1963 until 1974, with a fifth made by Holden for 2004 to 2006. The first generation is credited with popularizing the muscle car in the 1960s. In 1964 and 1965 it was an option package on the intermediate LeMans.

nuggets.text: The GTO name was inspired by the Ferrari 250 GTO.

cars.name: Ford Mustang (first generation)
cars.blurb: The first-generation Mustang was built by Ford from March 1964 until 1973, and it created a new class of cars known as pony cars. It was introduced on April 17, 1964 as a hardtop and convertible, with the fastback following in August 1964, on a platform shared with the Falcon. Its long hood and short deck proved wildly popular and inspired a host of competition.

nuggets.text: The car driven by McQueen, later owned by Robert Kiernan and then his son Sean, sold at Mecum Auctions on January 10, 2020 for a record $3.7 million, including auction fees.
Mustang sales began in 1964 with 22,000 orders taken on the first day, at the World's Fair and around the United States.

cars.name: Shelby Mustang
cars.blurb: The Shelby Mustang is a high-performance variant of the Ford Mustang, built by Shelby American from 1965 to 1967 and by Ford from 1968 to 1970. The GT350 debuted in 1965 in the fastback body of the first-generation Mustang. The 1965 car carried a full-size spare where the rear seats would be, which made it a two-seater so it could qualify as a sports car under SCCA regulations.

nuggets.text: A total of 34 race-spec GT350R cars were built specifically for competition under SCCA rules, and the model was B-Production champion three years running.
Hertz advertised its first 85 cars, which were available with four-speed manual transmissions, as "Rent-a-Racer" cars.

cars.name: Ford GT40
cars.blurb: The Ford GT40 was a mid-engined racing car built by Ford for 1960s European endurance racing, with the specific aim of beating Ferrari, which had won Le Mans six years running from 1960 to 1965. Around 100 were made, mostly 289 cu in V8 Mk Is. Ford won World Championship categories from 1966 to 1968, and the Gulf-entered Mk I won Le Mans in 1968 and 1969.

nuggets.text: At Le Mans in 1966 the Mk II broke Ferrari's winning streak, making Ford the first American manufacturer to win a major European race since Jimmy Murphy's Duesenberg in the 1921 French Grand Prix.
In 2018 RM Sotheby's sold a Mk II that finished third overall at Le Mans in 1966 for $9,795,000, the highest price paid at that time for a GT40 at auction.

cars.name: Chevrolet Camaro (first generation)
cars.blurb: The first-generation Camaro was Chevrolet's pony car, introduced in the fall of 1966 for the 1967 model year and built through 1969. It used a new rear-wheel-drive GM F-body platform, shared with the Pontiac Firebird, and came as a 2-door hardtop or convertible. A 230 cu in straight-6 was standard, with several Chevy V8s available as options.

nuggets.text: A Central Office Production Order was placed for the only Z/28 convertible Camaro built.

A 1968 Z/28 raced in the 1971 British Saloon Car Championship at Crystal Palace, in a three-way fight for the lead that the BBC later featured in the "Sporting Moments" episode of its 100 Greatest series.

specs.engine: 230 cuin L26 I6; 250 cuin L22 I6; 283 cuin small-block V8; 302 cuin Z28 V8 (Z/28); 307 cuin L14 V8; 327 cuin LF7/L30 V8; 350 cuin LM1/L65 V8; 350 cuin L48 V8 (SS350); 396 cuin L35/L34/L78 V8 (SS396); 427 cuin L72/ZL1 V8 (COPO)

cars.name: Chevrolet Chevelle
cars.blurb: The Chevelle was a mid-sized Chevrolet built in three generations for the 1964 to 1977 model years, on the GM A-body platform. It was the U.S. auto industry's only all-new car for 1964, placed between the small Chevy II and the full-sized Chevrolets, and it became one of Chevrolet's most successful nameplates. The Super Sport versions ran through 1973, and the Malibu replaced the Chevelle name from 1978.

nuggets.text: Driving his #11 Chevelle, Yarborough won nine of 30 starts and finished 386 points ahead of runner-up Richard Petty.
Only 200 regular-production 1965 Z-16 Chevelles were built, at the Kansas City plant.

cars.name: Plymouth Road Runner
cars.blurb: The Plymouth Road Runner was a muscle car introduced by Chrysler for the 1968 model year, first based on the mid-size Belvedere. It paired a powerful engine with spartan trim and a price that undercut costlier muscle cars such as the Pontiac GTO and Plymouth's own GTX, and it was initially a sales success. The nameplate became a trim package on the compact Volare in 1976 and was discontinued in 1980.

nuggets.text: Only three Hemi (R) code Road Runner convertibles were built, plus one that went to Canada.
Richard Petty won the championship in both 1971 and 1972 in Road Runner-based cars, taking 30 races over the two seasons.

cars.name: Plymouth Barracuda
cars.blurb: The Plymouth Barracuda was a two-door pony car built by Chrysler from 1964 through 1974. The first generation, 1964 to 1966, was a hardtop fastback on the A-body that shared most of its parts and bodywork with the Valiant, apart from its wraparound rear glass. The second generation, 1967 to 1969, was heavily redesigned, and the third, 1970 to 1974, shared the E-body with the Dodge Challenger.

nuggets.text: A few late-build 1971 convertibles, fitted with 1972 grilles and rear panels, went to Paramount Studios for TV and movie work and appeared on Mannix, The Brady Bunch and other shows.

cars.name: Dodge Charger (second generation)
cars.blurb: The Dodge Charger is a mid-size car built on the Chrysler B platform for the 1966 through 1978 model years.

cars.name: Dodge Challenger (first generation)
cars.blurb: The first-generation Dodge Challenger was a pony car built for the 1970 to 1974 model years on the Chrysler E platform, in hardtop and convertible styles, sharing major components with the Plymouth Barracuda. Carl Cameron is listed as its designer. Dodge had used the Challenger name earlier, in 1959, for a value version of the full-sized Coronet Silver Challenger. A total of 165,437 first-generation cars were sold.

nuggets.text: The T/A was one of the first U.S. muscle cars to run different size tires front and rear: E60x15 Goodyear Polyglas in front and G60x15 at the back.
Cameron based the 1970 Challenger grille on an older sketch of a stillborn 1966 Charger prototype that was to have had a turbine engine.

cars.name: Buick GNX
cars.blurb: The GNX is a high-performance Buick coupe built on the Regal, alongside the Grand National and the Gran Sport. Its performance changes included a GNX-specific EPROM, a low-restriction exhaust with dual mufflers, a reprogrammed turbo Hydramatic 200-4R with a custom torque converter and cooler, a unique differential cover, and a panhard rod. Among turbo Regals, only the GNX was rarer than the Turbo Regal Limited.

nuggets.text: The 2018 to 2020 Regal GS, the most powerful Regal ever produced, was the first in the model line to top the official rated power of the 1987 Buick GNX.
The GNX appears on the cover of Kendrick Lamar's 2024 album, which is titled GNX.

cars.name: DeLorean DMC-12
cars.blurb: The DeLorean is a rear-engine, two-seat sports car made by John DeLorean's company for the American market for the 1981 to 1983 model years, and it was the only car the company brought to market. Giorgetto Giugiaro designed it, and it is noted for gull-wing doors and brushed stainless-steel body panels, though its performance was relatively modest. Power came from the PRV V6, also used by Peugeot, Renault and Volvo.

nuggets.text: For Christmas 1980, a DeLorean and American Express promotion planned to sell 100 24K-gold-plated DeLoreans at $85,000 each to gold-card members, but only two were sold.
Two of the cars used in Back to the Future Part III were given Volkswagen engines and dune buggy chassis for the scenes filmed in the Western terrain.

cars.name: Cadillac Allante
cars.blurb: The Allante was a two-seat luxury convertible roadster sold by Cadillac for the 1987 to 1993 model years. It used a Cadillac chassis and mechanicals, while Pininfarina built the bodywork in Italy and airfreighted it to Detroit for final assembly. General Motors chose the name from 1,700 computer-generated candidates, and over 21,000 were made in seven years.

nuggets.text: Despite a scheduled facelift, the last Allante was flown from Turin, Italy on July 2, 1993 and completed at Detroit-Hamtramck 14 days later.
Traction control was added, the first front-wheel-drive car with a V8 to be so equipped.

cars.name: Dodge Viper
cars.blurb: The Dodge Viper was an American sports car first shown in 1989 as a concept inspired by a modern-era AC Cobra, with production beginning in 1991. Five generations were built through 2017. Early on it had a reputation as an intimidating car to drive, with high power and torque and no driver aids. Later electronic assists and safety features made it more accessible while performance kept rising.

nuggets.text: Kuno Wittmer drove a street-legal 2010 Viper ACR to a 1:59.995 lap at Miller Motorsports Park in Utah, the first time a production car broke the two-minute mark on the 3.048-mile Outer Course.
The car won its class at Le Mans three years running, in 1998, 1999 and 2000, took overall victory at the 2000 24 Hours of Daytona, and won the Spa 24 Hours in 2001 and 2002.

cars.name: GMC Syclone

photos.artist: Charles from Port Chester, New York

cars.blurb: The GMC Syclone was a high-performance version of the GMC Sonoma compact pickup, with a turbocharged 4.3 L V6 and four-wheel drive. GMC built it in 1991 with Production Automotive Services, the company credited with the 1989 Pontiac Turbo Trans Am, and it was the fastest production truck for 1991. The 1992 to 1993 Typhoon SUV, based on the GMC Jimmy, followed it.

nuggets.text: The Syclone was the first production truck to get a 4-wheel anti-lock braking system.
Three Indy Syclones were used at the Indianapolis 500 on May 24, 1992, with a sticker package as their only modification.

cars.name: Chevrolet Camaro (fourth generation)
cars.blurb: The fourth-generation Camaro was a Chevrolet pony car built for the 1993 through 2002 model years on an updated F-body platform. It kept the first generation's basic recipe: two doors, coupe or convertible, rear-wheel drive, and a choice of six-cylinder and V8 engines. It was revised in 1998 with exterior and engine changes, and discontinued because of slow sales, a deteriorated sports coupe market and plant overcapacity.

nuggets.text: The LT4 was the fastest factory-built Camaro available, and the most expensive at US$40,000.
The Camaro's LS1 used a cable-actuated throttle body instead of the Corvette's drive-by-wire, and 1998 was the only year LS1 models had a working coolant temperature gauge.

cars.name: Pontiac Firebird (fourth generation)
cars.blurb: The Pontiac Firebird was built by Pontiac from the 1967 to 2002 model years. The 1997 model year brought standard air conditioning, daytime running lamps using the front turn signals, a digital odometer, and an optional 500-watt Monsoon cassette or compact disc stereo to all Firebird trim levels.

cars.name: Ford Mustang (fourth generation)
cars.blurb: The fourth-generation Mustang, coded SN95, ran from the 1994 through 2004 model years and was the first major redesign of the Mustang in fifteen years. It was introduced in November 1993, with the launch on December 9, and rode on an updated Fox platform, the last car to use it. Bud Magaldi's styling borrowed from classic Mustangs, a convertible returned, and the coupe replaced the notchback and hatchback.

nuggets.text: Ford allocated US$700 million to improve the Fox platform for the 1994 Mustang.

Though capable of matching or exceeding the output of the older 302 V8, the 4.6 L V8 drew criticism for inadequate performance, particularly against the larger OHV V8 in the Mustang's chief rival, the Camaro.
