specs.designer: Bud Magaldi (exterior: 1990) ; Emeline King (interior: 1990) ; Doug Gaffka (facelift: 1996)

cars.name: Chevrolet Impala SS
cars.blurb: The 1994 to 1996 Impala SS was mechanically the same as the Caprice 9C1 with the 5.7 L V8, with both sharing four-wheel disc brakes and rigid heavy-duty suspension components. It was built at the Arlington, Texas plant that also built the Caprice, Buick Roadmaster, Oldsmobile Custom Cruiser and Cadillac Fleetwood.

nuggets.text: In 1995 and 1996 the Impala SS was exported to Middle Eastern markets as the Caprice SS, identical to the American car except for the side lettering on the rear quarter panel and the badge on the dashboard.

cars.name: Ford GT
cars.blurb: The Ford GT was a mid-engine sports car from Ford. Its first private sale was completed on August 4, 2004, when former Microsoft executive Jon Shirley took delivery of his Midnight Blue 2005 Ford GT. Installation of the engine and transmission, along with the seats and interior finishing, was handled in the SVT building at Ford's Wixom, Michigan plant.

nuggets.text: Shirley earned the right to buy the first production Ford GT, chassis #10, at a charity auction at the Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance, bidding over US$557,000.

cars.name: Porsche 356
cars.blurb: The Porsche 356 is a lightweight, nimble-handling rear-engine sports car and the first production Porsche, offered as a two-door coupe and in open form. Production began in 1948 at Gmund, Austria, where Porsche built about 50 cars, then moved to Zuffenhausen, Germany, in 1950. General production continued until April 1965, after the 911 had debuted in September 1964. About half of the 76,000 built survive.

nuggets.text: The first 356 was road certified in Austria on June 8, 1948, and was entered in a race in Innsbruck, where it won its class.
The last ten 356s, all cabriolets, were assembled in March 1966 as 1965 models for the Dutch Rijkspolitie, the highway patrol that preceded the Netherlands police force.

cars.name: Porsche 550 Spyder
cars.blurb: The Porsche 550 was a racing sports car built from 1953 until 1956, with only 90 made. It was a mid-engine car with an air-cooled four-cylinder engine, following the 1948 Porsche 356/1 prototype designed by Ferry Porsche. It quickly established dominance in the 1.1 and 1.5 liter classes, and won the Nurburgring Eifel Race in May 1953, the first race it entered.

nuggets.text: James Dean's 550, numbered 130 and one of the first 90 built, was involved in a collision at the Cholame Junction on September 30, 1955 that killed him.
A 1958 Porsche 550A Spyder sold at Bonhams in 2018 for $5,170,000, the highest price for a 550 at auction.

cars.name: Porsche 911 (classic)
cars.blurb: The original Porsche 911 is a rear-engined, air-cooled sports car from Porsche of Stuttgart. A prototype was shown to the public in autumn 1963, and production ran from September 1964 through 1989. It was succeeded by a modified version, internally called the 964 but still sold as a 911. The original series is often cited as the most successful competition car ever, especially counting variants such as the 935.

nuggets.text: The Porsche factory team used the 911E in rallies, and amateur entrants, who tended to buy the 911S, called it the "Secret weapon from Zuffenhausen."
Collectors value the Carrera RS models, which many consider the greatest classic 911s of all time.

specs.engine: 2.0 L air-cooled H6 ; 2.2 L air-cooled H6 ; 2.3 L air-cooled H6 ; 2.7 L air-cooled H6 ; 3.0 L air-cooled H6 ; 3.2 L air-cooled H6 ; 3.0 L air-cooled turbo H6 ; 3.3 L air-cooled turbo H6

cars.name: Porsche 914
cars.blurb: The Porsche 914 was a mid-engined sports car designed, built and sold jointly by Volkswagen and Porsche from 1969 to 1976. It was a targa-topped two-seater powered by either a flat-4 or a flat-six. Of 118,978 built, 115,646 were four-cylinder 914/4s and 3,332 were six-cylinder 914/6s.

nuggets.text: The 914 is renowned as Formula One's first safety car, deployed at the 1973 Canadian Grand Prix to help manage a race hit by incidents in treacherous weather.
A 914/6 GT driven by Claude Ballot-Lena and Guy Chasseuil won the GTS class and finished sixth overall at the 1970 24 Hours of Le Mans.

specs.engine: 1.7 L Volkswagen Type 4 F4; 1.8 L Volkswagen Type 4 F4; 2.0 L Volkswagen Type 4 F4; 2.0 L Type 901/36 F6 (914/6)

cars.name: Porsche 917
cars.blurb: The Porsche 917 was a sports prototype race car built to exploit the regulations for 5-litre sports cars, powered by a Type 912 flat-12 enlarged from 4.5 to 5.0 litres. Introduced in 1969, it was unwieldy at first, but development improved the handling and it dominated sports-car racing in 1970 and 1971. It gave Porsche its first overall Le Mans win in 1970 and repeated in 1971.

nuggets.text: The Martini Racing 917K of Helmut Marko and Gijs van Lennep, built with a magnesium frame, won and set an overall distance record that stood until 2010.
Porsche developed the 917 from the 908 in only ten months.

specs.engine: 4494 cc Type 912 Flat-12 ; 4999 cc Type 912 Flat-12 ; 5374 cc Type 912 Flat-12

cars.name: Porsche 930 Turbo
cars.blurb: The 930 was the turbocharged 911, built by Porsche in Stuttgart-Zuffenhausen from 1975 to 1989. It stayed at the top of the 911 range for its whole production run and, when it arrived, was the fastest production car in Germany. The 3.0-litre cars ran from 1975 to 1977, with 2,819 built, and the 3.3-litre followed from 1978.

nuggets.text: Car and Driver timed both the 1975 and 1978 Turbo at 4.9 seconds to 60 mph, and the two shared first place in the magazine's ranking of the quickest cars of the 1970s.
Ferry Porsche gave the first Turbo model to his sister Louise Piëch for her 70th birthday.

specs.engine: 3.0 L 930/50 air-cooled turbo H6 ; 3.3 L 930/60 air-cooled turbo H6

cars.name: Porsche 944

photos.artist: Charles from Port Chester, New York

cars.blurb: The 944 was a front-engine, rear-drive Porsche built from 1982 to 1991 on the platform of the 924, offered as a coupé or cabriolet. It came with naturally aspirated or turbocharged engines, and more than 163,000 were produced, making it the most successful sports car in Porsche's history until the Boxster and 997 Carrera arrived. For 1992 it was revised and renamed the 968.

nuggets.text: The 944 Turbo was the first car to offer airbags as standard equipment. On other 944 models they were optional.
The 944 Turbo S was the fastest production four-cylinder car of its time.

cars.name: Porsche 959
cars.blurb: The 959 began as a Group B rally car and became a road-legal Porsche built from 1986 to 1993, meeting an FIA rule that required at least 200 units. It paired a twin-turbocharged flat-six with all-wheel drive and a six-speed manual. At 317 km/h it was the world's fastest street-legal production car when introduced, and many consider it the most technologically advanced road car of its time.

nuggets.text: The six-speed gearbox had a first gear labelled "gelände", meaning terrain, which let the car pass noise regulations.

Porsche designed and tested the 959 to European safety standards only, ignoring NHTSA standards, when it was already apparent that the exchange rate was so poor that Porsche was losing $200,000 on each sale.

cars.name: Porsche 911 (964)
cars.blurb: The 964 reworked the 911 for 1989 with significant styling revisions, most visibly more integrated bumpers. It was the first car offered with Porsche's Tiptronic automatic transmission and all-wheel drive as options. The earliest cars were all-wheel-drive Carrera 4 models, and the rear-drive Carrera 2 joined the range in 1990. In all, 63,762 cars were built.

nuggets.text: The Turbo S LM-GT debuted at the 1993 12 Hours of Sebring, where it finished seventh overall and first in its class with the Brumos Porsche racing team (Röhrl, Stuck and Haywood).
Porsche planned to build 3000 of the 1994 Speedsters in 1992, but only 936 were built and sold over two years of production.

cars.name: Porsche 911 (993)
cars.blurb: The 993 is the fourth-generation 911, sold from 1994 to 1998 and the last of the air-cooled cars. Tony Hatter drew the exterior, with much more flared wheel arches over the core body shell of the 964. Porsche says only 20% of its parts carried over from the previous 911. It was also the first 911 with a six-speed gearbox as standard.

nuggets.text: The last 993, and so the last air-cooled 911 built for public roads, was a Riviera Blue Carrera 4 S completed on 31 March 1998. Its owner was American TV star Jerry Seinfeld.
Seinfeld also ordered the last US-bound 993, a black Carrera 2 S completed in December 1997.

specs.engine: 3.6 L M64 air-cooled SOHC H6 ; 3.8 L M64/20 air-cooled SOHC H6 ; 3.6 L M64/60 air-cooled twin-turbo SOHC H6

cars.name: Porsche 911 (996)
cars.blurb: The 996 is the fifth-generation 911, built from 1997 to 2006 and a complete break from the original car apart from its overall layout. It brought the first all-new chassis since the original 911 and a new water-cooled engine. Development was shared with the Boxster, and the two cars have the front suspension, engine and various interior parts in common.

nuggets.text: A Mk.II GT3 tested in 2004 produced 1.03 g on the skidpad, the second highest figure ever recorded by a street-legal vehicle at the time.
The 996 Turbo's water-cooled twin-turbocharged 3.6-litre flat-six was derived from the engine of the 1998 Le Mans winning 911 GT1 race car.

specs.production: July 17, 1997–2004 (2005 and 2006 for 911 Turbo S, GT2 and GT3 models only)
specs.engine: 3.4 L–3.6 L M96 naturally aspirated/twin-turbocharged flat-6

cars.name: Porsche Carrera GT

photos.artist: Brian Snelson from Hockley, Essex, England

cars.blurb: The Carrera GT was a mid-engine Porsche sports car built in Leipzig from 2003 to 2006, with 1,270 made. It had a 5,733 cc V10, rear-wheel drive, a six-speed manual and a two-door Targa roadster body. Sports Car International named it number one on its list of Top Sports Cars of the 2000s and number eight of all time, and Popular Science gave it a Best of What's New award in 2003.

specs.layout: Longitudinally mounted rear mid-engine, rear-wheel drive

cars.name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SL
cars.blurb: The 300 SL was a two-seat Mercedes-Benz built from 1954 to 1957 as a gullwing coupé and from 1957 to 1963 as a roadster, 3,258 cars in all. Its three-litre straight-six was among the first car engines with mechanical direct gasoline fuel injection, and the car traced back to the 1952 racing 300 SL, the W194. Depending on its set-up it could reach 260 km/h.

nuggets.text: Only 29 were made with the expensive all-aluminum body.

cars.name: BMW M1
cars.blurb: The BMW M1 was a mid-engine coupé built from 1978 to 1981, styled by Giorgetto Giugiaro at Italdesign. Lamborghini first agreed to build a production racing car in sufficient quantity for homologation, but conflicts led BMW to build it themselves. Its 3.5-litre straight-six drove the rear wheels through a five-speed manual, and only 453 were made. It was the first mid-engine BMW to be mass-produced.

nuggets.text: In June 1979 Hervé Poulain, Manfred Winkelhock and Marcel Mignot raced an M1 Art Car, its body painted by Andy Warhol, at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the IMSA GTX class.
The Procar BMW M1 Championship ran as a Formula One support series and put many F1 drivers in identical cars.

cars.name: Volkswagen Beetle
cars.blurb: The Beetle, officially the Volkswagen Type 1, was built from 1938 to 2003, a run of 65 years that is the longest for any single generation of automobile. Ferdinand Porsche and his team developed it as a people's car, inexpensive, simple and mass-produced, after Adolf Hitler decided Germany needed one. With 21.5 million made, it is the best-selling car of a single platform in history.

nuggets.text: On 17 February 1972 the Beetle broke the world record for best-selling automobile, with 15,007,034 built, passing the Ford Model T's figure that had stood for nearly 50 years.
Starting with The Love Bug, one of the top grossing movies of 1969, Herbie became a fixture of popular culture and was partly responsible for boosting Beetle sales in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

cars.name: Volkswagen Golf Mk1
cars.blurb: The Golf Mk1 was the Beetle's successor, debuting in Europe in May 1974 with styling by Giorgetto Giugiaro's Italdesign. It marked Volkswagen's shift from rear-wheel drive and rear-mounted air-cooled engines to front-wheel drive with front-mounted, water-cooled engines. In the United States and Canada it was introduced in December 1974 as the Volkswagen Rabbit, and in Mexico it was the Caribe.

nuggets.text: Volkswagen's chief of research Ernst Fiala drove a prototype, objected to the harsh suspension and excessive intake noise, and declared the car "undriveable".
The Mk1 Golf GTI took international rally wins in Sweden (1978, 1982, 1983), Monte Carlo (1980), Great Britain (1983) and Portugal (1984).

cars.name: Audi Quattro
cars.blurb: The Audi Quattro is both a road car and a rally car, first shown at the 1980 Geneva Motor Show on 3 March. It used Audi's quattro permanent four-wheel drive system, with a turbocharged inline-five at the front. Production ran until 1991 and reached 11,452 cars. The original model is often called the Ur-Quattro.

nuggets.text: In 1981 Michèle Mouton became the first female driver to win a world championship rally, driving an Audi Quattro.
The S1 E2 was the last Group B car Audi produced, and the works team withdrew from the championship after the 1986 rally in Portugal.

specs.designer: Jörg Bensinger ; Walter Treser ; Ferdinand Piëch ; Franz Tengler (transmission) ; Martin Smith (exterior styling)

cars.name: Jaguar E-Type
cars.blurb: The E-Type, sold as the XK-E in North America, was a British front-engined Jaguar sports car built from 1961 to 1974. It was based on the D-Type racing car. Its claimed 150 mph top speed, sub-7-second 0 to 60 mph time, largely unitary body, independent suspension at both ends with disc brakes, and rack-and-pinion steering spurred industry-wide changes. Malcolm Sayer was the designer.

nuggets.text: In 1996 New York's Museum of Modern Art added a blue E-Type roadster to its permanent design collection, one of only six automobiles to receive the distinction.
A 1963 E-Type Lightweight Competition, one of just twelve built, sold for $7,370,000 at the 2017 Scottsdale, Arizona auctions.

cars.name: Aston Martin DB4 GT Zagato
cars.blurb: The DB4 GT Zagato was a grand tourer produced from 1960 to 1963 and introduced at the London Motor Show in October 1960. Ercole Spada of Zagato lightened and improved the DB4 GT in Italy. The factory first planned 25 cars, but demand was weaker than expected and production fell to 19. Later cars called Sanction II and Sanction III were made with the Zagato works, and unauthorised replicas exist.

nuggets.text: At a British Grand Prix support race in July 1961 the Zagato had its first victory, with 2 VEV taking the lead on the last lap from a Jaguar E-Type.

specs.production: 1960–1963; (25 produced, inc 4 Sanction II and 2 Sanction III)

cars.name: Aston Martin DB5
cars.blurb: The DB5 is a British grand tourer built by Aston Martin from 1963 to 1965, designed by Carrozzeria Touring Superleggera and powered by a 3,995 cc Marek straight-six. It evolved from the last series of the DB4, and 1,059 were made. It is best known for its role in the James Bond films, where the fictional spy first drove one in Goldfinger (1964).

nuggets.text: Chassis DP/216/1 was stolen in 1997 from its last owner in Florida and was reported to be still missing in 2021.
The second publicity car, DB5/2008/R, was auctioned by RM Sotheby's in August 2019 for $6.4 million to an unknown buyer.

specs.designer: Federico Formenti at Carrozzeria Touring Superleggera

cars.name: Lotus Esprit
cars.blurb: The Lotus Esprit was a rear mid-engine, rear-drive sports car built at Hethel from 1976 to 2004, and 10,675 were made. Giorgetto Giugiaro drew it in his sharp-creased "folded paper" style, and its backbone chassis was later adapted to carry the DeLorean. With the Elise and Exige, it is one of Lotus's longest-lived models.

nuggets.text: The nameless prototype, often called "the Silver Car", appeared on the Italdesign stand at the 1972 Turin Auto Show, and the positive reception convinced Chapman to approve further development.
After 28 years the last Esprit left the line on 20 February 2004 and was shipped to Chicago.

cars.name: McLaren F1
cars.blurb: The McLaren F1 was the first type-approved road car from the Formula One team. Gordon Murray's concept was styled by Peter Stevens, and BMW built a 6,064 cc V12 for it. It was one of the first sports cars with a fully carbon-fibre monocoque body and chassis structure, and it seated three adults. It was recognised as the world's fastest production car at launch, and was the last road-legal, series-produced sports car to win Le Mans outright.

nuggets.text: Gordon Murray's design for the F1's doors was inspired by the Toyota Sera.
The F1 LM once held the 0 to 100 to 0 mph record, completing it in 11.5 seconds with Andy Wallace driving at the disused RAF Alconbury airbase.

specs.designer: Gordon Murray ; Peter Stevens ; Paul Rosche (engine designer) (BMW)

cars.name: Mini
cars.blurb: The Mini was a small two-door, four-seat car designed by Sir Alec Issigonis, built from 1959 to 2000 over a single generation. It first sold as the Austin Seven and Morris Mini-Minor and became a marque in its own right in 1969. About 5.38 million were built, and the Cooper and Cooper S won the Monte Carlo Rally in 1964, 1965 and 1967.

nuggets.text: By July 1957 the original prototype, XC9003, had been designed and built. It was affectionately named the "Orange Box" because of its colour.
The last Mini, a red Cooper Sport, was built on 4 October 2000 and presented to the British Motor Industry Heritage Trust that December.

specs.body_style: 2-door saloon ; 2-door convertible ; 2-door estate ; 2-door van ; 2-door coupe utility

cars.name: Citroen DS
cars.blurb: The Citroën DS was built from 1955 to 1975, with 1,455,746 produced. Flaminio Bertoni and André Lefèbvre styled and engineered it, and it was known for an aerodynamic, futuristic shape and quirky, innovative technology. It was the first mass-production car with both hydropneumatic suspension and disc brakes, and the 1967 Series 3 brought directional headlights to mass production.

nuggets.text: At the show, 743 orders were taken in the first 15 minutes, and orders for the first day totalled 12,000.
In the 1974 London-Sahara-Munich World Cup Rally the DS won against more than 70 other cars, only 5 of which completed the whole event.

specs.designer: Flaminio Bertoni ; André Lefèbvre ; Robert Opron (1967 facelift)

cars.name: Bugatti Type 35
cars.blurb: The Bugatti Type 35 was a race car built at Molsheim from 1924 to 1930, designed by Ettore Bugatti around a straight-eight engine. It pioneered the idea of a race-ready car available for purchase, and privateers around the world bought it. Its egg-shaped radiator and tapered tail are emblematic. It won over 1,000 races and took the Grand Prix World Championship in 1926.

nuggets.text: A British Racing Green Type 35B driven by William Grover-Williams won the inaugural 1929 Monaco Grand Prix.

cars.name: Bugatti Veyron
cars.blurb: The Bugatti Veyron EB 16.4 is a mid-engine, all-wheel-drive sports car developed in Germany by the Volkswagen Group and Bugatti and built in Molsheim, France, from 2005 to 2015. Its 7,993 cc quad-turbocharged W16 gave the original version a top speed of 407 km/h. The Super Sport is one of the fastest street-legal production cars in the world. In all, 450 were built.

nuggets.text: The Veyron is named for Pierre Veyron, a Bugatti development engineer, test driver and race driver who won the 1939 24 Hours of Le Mans in a Bugatti with co-driver Jean-Pierre Wimille.
The final production Veyron, a Grand Sport Vitesse titled "La Finale", was displayed at the Geneva Motor Show from 5 to 15 March 2015.

specs.body_style: 2-door coupé (16.4, Super Sport) ; 2-door targa top (Grand Sport, Grand Sport Vitesse)

cars.name: Toyota 2000GT

photos.artist: Shelby Asistio from Los Angeles, United States
Steve Ginn from Ventura California, United States

cars.blurb: The Toyota 2000GT was a front mid-engine, rear-drive two-seater designed by Toyota with Yamaha, shown at the 1965 Tokyo Motor Show and built by Yamaha from 1967 to 1970. Only 337 regular production cars were built, and according to Toyota all of them sold. Reviewing a pre-production car in 1967, Road & Track called it one of the most exciting and enjoyable cars it had driven.

nuggets.text: A custom open-top 2000GT was built for the James Bond film You Only Live Twice, yet a factory convertible was never offered.
In 2022 one of the Toyota-Shelby 2000GTs sold at auction for US $2.5 million.

specs.engine: Gasoline: ; 2.0 L 3M DOHC I6 (MF10) ; 2.3 L 2M-B SOHC I6 (MF12)

cars.name: Nissan Skyline GT-R
cars.blurb: The Nissan Skyline GT-R is a Japanese grand tourer based on the Skyline range. The first cars to carry the name were built from 1969 to 1972 as the KPGC10 and did well in Japanese touring car racing. A brief second generation followed in 1973, then the name returned in 1989 after a 16-year gap as the R32. Group A R32s won the Japanese Touring Car Championship four years in a row.

nuggets.text: The technology and performance of the R32 GT-R prompted the Australian publication Wheels to nickname the GT-R "Godzilla" in its July 1989 edition.
Before the R33 was officially released, Dirk Schoysman drove one around the Nürburgring Nordschleife in 7:59.887, described as the first production vehicle to break into the sub-8-minute mark.

cars.name: Mazda MX-5
cars.blurb: The Mazda MX-5 is a lightweight two-seat sports car, sold in the United States as the MX-5 Miata and in Japan as the Roadster. Built at Mazda's Hiroshima plant, it debuted at the 1989 Chicago Auto Show under the design credo Jinba ittai, meaning unity of horse and rider. The Lotus Elan served as a design benchmark. More than a million have been sold, the best-selling two-seat convertible sports car in history.

nuggets.text: In 2000 the Guinness Book of World Records declared the MX-5 the best-selling two-seat sports car in history, with total production then at 531,890 units.
The Duo 101 won the competition at its second round in August 1984, when full-scale clay models were presented, and was selected as the basis for what would become the MX-5.

cars.name: Honda NSX
cars.blurb: The first-generation Honda NSX is a two-seat, mid-engine sports car built by Honda in Japan from 1990 to 2005, and sold in North America and Hong Kong as the Acura NSX. The name began as NS-X, short for New Sportscar eXperimental. Power came from a transversely mounted V6, 2,977 cc in the C30A and 3,179 cc in the C32B.

nuggets.text: Formula One driver Ayrton Senna consulted with the NSX's chief engineers while testing the prototype at Honda's Suzuka Circuit in the final stages of suspension tuning.
Only 30 NSX Type-S Zeros were produced between 1997 and 2001, making it the rarest version of the NSX next to the five homologation special NSX-R GT cars.

specs.engine: 2977 cc Honda C30A V6 ; 3179 cc Honda C32B V6
specs.designer: Ken Okuyama (1987) ; Masahito Nakano (1987) ; Shigeru Uehara (1988) ; James Stevens (1988)

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Silver Ghost
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Silver Ghost name refers both to a car model and one specific car from that series. Originally named the "40/50 h.p." the chassis was first made at Royce's Manchester works, with production moving to Derby in July 1908, and also, between 1921 and 1926, in Springfield, Massachusetts, USA. Chassis no. 60551, registered AX 201, was the car that was originally given the name "Silver Ghost". Other 40/50 hp cars were also given names, but the Silver Ghost title was taken up by the press, and soon all 40/50s were called by the name, a fact not officially recognised by Rolls-Royce until 1925, when the Phantom range was launched.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Phantom I
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Phantom was Rolls-Royce's replacement for the original Silver Ghost. Introduced as the New Phantom in 1925, the Phantom had a larger engine than the Silver Ghost and used pushrod-operated overhead valves instead of the Silver Ghost's side valves. The Phantom was built in Derby, England, and Springfield, Massachusetts, in the United States.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Phantom III
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Phantom III was the final large pre-war Rolls-Royce. Introduced in 1936, it replaced the Phantom II, and it was the only V12 Rolls-Royce until the 1998 introduction of the Silver Seraph.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Phantom IV
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Phantom IV is a British automobile produced by Rolls-Royce. Only eighteen were made between 1950 and 1956, sold only to buyers whom Rolls-Royce considered worthy of the distinction: the British royal family and heads of state. Sixteen are known to still exist in museums as well as in public and private collections.

specs.engine: 5.7 L I8 (first 15 vehicles) ; 6.5 L I8 (final 3 vehicles)

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Silver Cloud
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Silver Cloud is a luxury automobile produced by Rolls-Royce Limited from April 1955 to March 1966. It was the core model of the Rolls-Royce range during that period. The Silver Cloud replaced the Silver Dawn and was, in turn, replaced by the Silver Shadow. The John P. Blatchley design was a major change from the pre-war models and the highly derivative Silver Dawn. As part of a range rationalisation, the Bentley S1 was made essentially identical, apart from its radiator grille and badging.

specs.engine: Mk.I: 4.9 L I6; Mk.II & III: 6.2 L V8

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Phantom V
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Phantom V is a large four-door limousine produced by Rolls-Royce Limited from 1959 to 1968. Based on the Silver Cloud II, it shares a V8 engine and Rolls-Royce Hydramatic automatic gearbox (manufactured under licence from General Motors by Rolls-Royce) with that model.

specs.designer: John Polwhele Blatchley of Park Ward for design #980 and Mulliner Park Ward design #2003 et al; A. F. McNeil of James Young for designs #PV10, PV15, PV16, PV22 et al.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Silver Shadow
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Silver Shadow and its slightly stretched version, the Rolls-Royce Silver Wraith II, are full-size luxury cars produced by British automaker Rolls-Royce in various forms from 1965 to 1980. It was the first of the marque to use fully slabsided unitary body and chassis construction, as well as all-around independent suspension. Two-door versions were initially, between 1965 and 1971, sold as the Rolls-Royce Silver Shadow 2-door saloon and the Silver Shadow Drophead Coupé, before they became the Rolls-Royce Corniche Coupé and Convertible, respectively. The Silver Shadow was produced from 1965 to 1976, and the Silver Shadow II from 1977 to 1980.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Phantom VI
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Phantom VI is a British limousine made from 1968 to 1990 by Rolls-Royce. A total of 374 Phantom VIs were made, of which fewer than 40 were manufactured in the last decade of production. The exterior is nearly identical to the facelifted Phantom V, on which it was based.

specs.engine: 6.2-litre (380 cubic inch) Rolls-Royce V8 (1968–1978); 6.75-litre (412 cubic inch) Rolls-Royce V8 (1979–1990)
specs.body_style: Limousines and other styles to buyer's choice

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Corniche
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Corniche is a two-door, front-engine, rear wheel drive luxury car produced by Rolls-Royce Motors as a hardtop coupé (from 1971 to 1980) and as a convertible (from 1971 to 1995 and 1999 to 2002). The Corniche was a development of the Mulliner Park Ward two-door versions of the Rolls-Royce Silver Shadow.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Camargue
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Camargue is a 2-door luxury saloon manufactured and marketed by Rolls-Royce Motors from 1975–1986.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Phantom (2003)
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Phantom is a full-sized luxury saloon car made by Rolls-Royce Motor Cars. Launched in 2003, it was the first Rolls-Royce developed and introduced after BMW purchased the right to use the Rolls-Royce name and logo in 1998. It was the seventh Rolls-Royce design to use the Phantom nameplate.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Cullinan
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Cullinan is a full-size luxury crossover sport utility vehicle (SUV)/4x4 manufactured by Rolls-Royce Motor Cars as the brand's first all-wheel drive vehicle. It is named after the Cullinan Diamond, the largest gem-quality rough diamond ever discovered.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Spectre
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Spectre is a full-sized luxury electric grand tourer manufactured by Rolls-Royce Motor Cars. The Spectre was formally launched in Napa Valley, California in 2023. The first deliveries of the car were made in the last quarter of 2023. It is Rolls-Royce's first electric vehicle (EV) and rides on the same platform as the Phantom and Cullinan.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Silver Wraith
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Silver Wraith was the first post-war Rolls-Royce. It was made from 1946 to 1958 as only a chassis at the company's Crewe factory, its former Merlin engine plant, alongside the shorter Bentley Mark VI. The Bentley was also available as a chassis for coachbuilders, but for the first time could be bought with a Rolls-Royce built Standard Steel body.

specs.body_style: Mostly 4-door saloons, but other body styles were erected on this chassis.

cars.name: Rolls-Royce Phantom II
cars.blurb: The Rolls-Royce Phantom II was the third and last of Rolls-Royce's 40/50 hp models, replacing the New Phantom in 1929. It used an improved version of the New Phantom engine in an all-new chassis. A "Continental" version, with a short wheelbase and stiffer springs, was offered.

cars.name: Bentley 3 Litre
cars.blurb: The Bentley 3 Litre was a car chassis manufactured by Bentley. The company's first, it was developed from 1919 and made available to customers' coachbuilders from 1921 to 1929. The Bentley was very much larger than the 1368 cc Bugattis that dominated racing at the time, but double the size of engine and strength compensated for the extra weight. The 4000 lb (1800 kg) car won the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1924, with drivers John Duff and Frank Clement, and again in 1927, this time in Super Sports form, with drivers S. C. H. "Sammy" Davis and Dudley Benjafield. Its weight, size, and speed prompted Ettore Bugatti to call it "the fastest lorry in the world", which was regarded as a compliment.

specs.body_style: as arranged with coachbuilder by customer

cars.name: Bentley 4½ Litre and Blower
cars.blurb: The Bentley 4½ Litre is a British car based on a rolling chassis built by Bentley Motors. Walter Owen Bentley replaced the Bentley 3 Litre with a more powerful car by increasing its engine displacement to 4.4 litres (270 cubic inches). A racing variant was known as the Blower Bentley. Bentley buyers used their cars for personal transport and arranged for their new chassis to be fitted with various body styles, mostly saloons or tourers. However, the publicity brought by their competition programme was invaluable for marketing Bentley's cars.

specs.engine: 4.4 L SOHC I4; 4.4 L supercharged SOHC I4
specs.body_style: as arranged with coachbuilder by customer

cars.name: Bentley Speed Six

photos.artist: Craig Howell from San Carlos, CA, USA

cars.blurb: The Bentley 6½ Litre and the high-performance Bentley Speed Six were rolling chassis produced by Bentley from 1926 to 1930. The Speed Six, introduced in 1928, became the most successful racing Bentley. Two Bentley Speed Sixes chassis became known as the Blue Train Bentleys after their owner Woolf Barnato in March 1930 "raced" the French Blue Train which departed Cannes at 17:45 and, after a stop in Paris, was scheduled to arrive in Calais at 15:24 when Barnato already was in his club in London.

specs.body_style: as arranged with coachbuilder by customer

cars.name: Bentley Mark VI
cars.blurb: The Bentley Mark VI is an automobile from Bentley which was produced from 1946 until 1952. The Mark VI 4-door standard steel sports saloon was the first post-war luxury car from Bentley. Announced in May 1946 and produced from 1946 to 1952 it was also both the first car from Rolls-Royce with all-steel coachwork and the first complete car assembled and finished at their factory.

specs.body_style: 4-door saloon; 2-door saloon; 2-door drophead coupé; chassis only (for coachbuilt bodies)

cars.name: Bentley R-Type Continental
cars.blurb: The R-Type Continental was a high-performance version of the R-Type. The early car has essentially the same engine as the standard R Type, but with modified carburation, induction and exhaust manifolds along with higher gear ratios. Most of the 207 cars produced were right-hand drive, with 43 left-hand drive examples produced for use abroad.

cars.name: Bentley Mulsanne (1980)
cars.blurb: The Bentley Mulsanne is a large (performance) luxury saloon produced by Bentley Motors from 1980 until 1992, though derivative models including the Continental T and Azure continued in production into the 2000s. Contrary to its predecessors, the Bentley Mulsanne was given an actual name instead of a letter, but otherwise started as another standard rebadged Rolls-Royce, the Silver Spirit.

specs.engine: 6.75 L Bentley V8; 6.75 L turbo Bentley V8 (1982–1985)

cars.name: Bentley Turbo R
cars.blurb: The Bentley Turbo R is a high-performance automobile which was produced by Bentley Motors Limited from 1985 to 1999. The "R" stood for "roadholding", to set it apart from its predecessor. It initially inherited the turbocharged engine from the Mulsanne Turbo and also sported a retuned suspension and wider tyres on aluminium alloy wheels, a first for a Bentley. From the 1987 model year (20,000 series chassis numbers), however, the Turbo R's V8 engine was retuned with fuel injection for added torque.

specs.production: Turbo R:1985–1997 ; 7,230 produced ; Turbo RT: 1997–1999 ; 252 produced

cars.name: Bentley Continental GT (2003)
cars.blurb: The Bentley Continental GT is a grand touring car from Bentley Motors. It is equipped with a 6.0 litre twin-turbocharged W12 engine.

cars.name: Bentley Speed 8
cars.blurb: The Bentley Speed 8 (developed from the Bentley EXP Speed 8) is a Grand Touring Prototype race car that was designed by Bentley. It has a strong resemblance to and shares some technology with the Audi R8C, which had raced only once before Audi dropped the project to focus on the later dominant Audi R8. The EXP Speed 8 marked Bentley's return to racing after a 73-year absence.

cars.name: Bentley Bentayga
cars.blurb: The Bentley Bentayga is a luxury SUV produced by British marque Bentley Motors. Introduced in late 2015, it is the brand's first luxury crossover SUV. Its unibody is manufactured at the Volkswagen Zwickau-Mosel Plant in Germany, then painted and assembled at Bentley's factory in Crewe, United Kingdom.
